findings.claim: None of the 72 cells (our 36 strategies at 15m and at 30m) shows a positive every-signal result that survives multiple testing. Averaged over all 36 strategies, the every-signal result is negative at both timeframes, and the 95% interval stays below zero.
findings.evidence: Every SUBMITTED signal run alone through the house exits: v3a = entered trades + nightly skipped shadows converted to R; v3b and v4 = replay. Pooled 15m: n 2,523, mean -0.235R, 4h-cluster bootstrap CI -0.370..-0.081, win 53.0%. Pooled 30m: n 1,115, mean -0.205R, CI -0.291..-0.111, win 58.6%. Positive cells after BH: 0 of 52 testable. Negative cells after BH (q<0.05): 13. Cells with n>=20: 35 of 41 have a negative mean, 15 have a CI entirely below 0, 0 have a CI entirely above 0. Sources: pooled_15_30.csv, cards_15_30.csv, summary_stats.txt (scripts cards.py, summary_stats.py).
findings.implication: With the house exits, the 15m/30m rule signals lose money. An AI trader on any of them starts from a negative base and has to create the edge itself, through which trades it takes and how it exits. Choosing the strategy does not hand it an edge.

findings.claim: Live matches the 5-year backtest. The 5-year every-signal result is negative in 69 of the 70 cells that had signals. In both live and 5-year data the loss per trade is about the round-trip cost: gross directional edge is roughly zero.
findings.evidence: 5-year (fiveyear_ref, profiles_binance): 69/70 cells have mean net return per notional below 0, 65 have t < -2, and 67 are negative in both the IS and CF windows. Median net per notional: 5-year -0.141% vs live every-signal -0.149% (41 cells with n>=20). Median 5-year gross per notional (net + 0.14% round trip): -0.002%. Live later runs (v3b+v4), gross R before fees and slippage: 15m +0.102R (CI -0.115..+0.393), 30m +0.008R (CI -0.117..+0.165). Fees+funding: 0.165R (15m) and 0.116R (30m). Slippage: 0.066R and 0.046R. Net: -0.130R and -0.154R. Signal generation is faithful: live vs 5-year signals/day Spearman 0.979, median ratio 0.95 (60 cells). Sources: gross_ci.py, summary_stats.txt.
findings.implication: The 5-year numbers are a trustworthy prior for these entries. Just to break even, an AI trader needs about 0.23R per trade of added value at 15m and about 0.16R at 30m (the median cost share). Nothing in the rule data shows such value exists yet.

findings.claim: By the pre-set tier rules, no cell is A. 4 cells are B, all at 30m: N10_HA_PSAR, S4_BB_BBP, N20_EMA9_CHOP and N24_DMI. 22 are D and 46 are C; 8 of the C cells never fired live. Every B cell's confidence interval includes zero.
findings.evidence: Rules were fixed before reading the results. A = n>=30, mean>0, CI lower bound >0, positive in every run with n>=5 (at least 2 runs), side-flip excess >0, and 5-year not negative. D = n>=20, mean<0, 5-year negative (t<-2), and either negative in every run with n>=5 or CI upper bound <0. B = n>=20, mean>0, positive in most runs. Everything else is C. The B cells: N10_HA_PSAR@30m +0.088R [-0.094,+0.253] n 49. S4_BB_BBP@30m +0.110R [-0.179,+0.413] n 42. N20_EMA9_CHOP@30m +0.086R [-0.269,+0.458] n 56. N24_DMI@30m +0.007R [-0.293,+0.246] n 44. A is impossible here because the 5-year result is negative in 69/70 cells. Source: cards_15_30.csv (tier column), cards.py.
findings.implication: None of the 36 strategies at 15m/30m is a verified non-loser, so none meets the owners' goal today. Any AI trader built on them is an experiment, not the deployment of a proven strategy.

findings.claim: Rankings do not carry over from one run to the next. Every cell that was positive in v3a turned negative later. No cell is positive in all three runs; 11 are negative in all three.
findings.evidence: Every-signal mean R, v3a vs v3b+v4 (33 cells with n>=10 in both): Spearman -0.131 (p 0.47). The 4 cells positive in v3a (N09_ALLIG_AROON@15m, N12_ICHI_AO@15m, S4_BB_BBP@30m, N10_HA_PSAR@30m) were all negative later. v3b vs v4: Spearman -0.111 (19 cells). The same-side-relative measure also fails to carry over (Spearman -0.07 to +0.13). Of 29 cells with n>=5 in all runs, 0 are positive in all three and 11 are negative in all three. Sources: summary_stats.txt and the per-run columns of cards_15_30.csv.
findings.implication: A November promotion based on a few weeks of account P&L will mostly pick noise. Promotion should rest on every-signal results with time-cluster CIs and criteria fixed in advance. For a +-0.1R interval a cell needs roughly 11-14 days of every-signal data at best (N04_ST_KLINGER@15m, N10_HA_PSAR@30m) and 30-60+ days for typical cells (column es_days_for_ci_halfwidth_0.1R).

findings.claim: The 36 strategies show no ability to pick the right direction at 15m/30m. The only raw-significant side-flip cells are short-only or short-heavy strategies, and the market fell during v3b and v4. Once the run's same-side drift is removed, their excess is about zero.
findings.evidence: Pipeline side-flip (coinflip_sideflip.csv), kind level: 15m +0.0066R (n 1,087, p 0.46), 30m -0.0227R (n 536, p 0.65). Raw p<0.05 cells: N20_EMA9_CHOP@15m +0.28R, N20_EMA9_CHOP@30m +0.36R (long share 0.00), N24_DMI@30m +0.29R (long share 0.11). Minus the mean of other strategies' same-side flips in the same run x tf, these become -0.065, +0.059 and +0.015R (sideflip_pairs_15_30.csv). Equal-weight market: v3b -0.9%, v4 -2.6%. A day-level drift benchmark was tried first and dropped because it produced absurd adjustments (N17_KC_RSI@15m +0.88R).
findings.implication: Do not treat N20_EMA9_CHOP or N24_DMI's recent wins as skill. As AI traders they would be short-side regime bets, and they need a regime rule plus testing in a rising market before any real money.

findings.claim: Under the house ladder, which locks profit at ROE levels, R per signal falls as leverage rises. In addition, 50x with margin equal to the leverage percentage can almost never be sized with a 2 ATR stop at 15m/30m.
findings.evidence: Fixed-leverage replay of all 1,891 15m/30m signals from v3b+v4 (levreplay.py, using the repo's obsshadows.variant_settings). Paired with the live rule on the same closed signals, 15m: 10x +0.162R (n 1,036), 20x +0.061R, 30x +0.018R, 40x -0.087R (n 926), 50x -0.404R (n 176). 30m: 10x +0.019R, 20x +0.061R, 30x +0.005R, 40x -0.001R. Share of signals that can be sized: 40x 78% (15m) and 33% (30m); 50x 14.3% (15m) and 0% (30m). Rejection reasons: loss at stop > 15% of equity, stop too close to liquidation, and the inferred brackets. Mark-inclusive mean R at 15m: 10x -0.020, live -0.128. Source: levreplay_summary.csv.
findings.implication: With house stops, the plan of 20-50x by AI confidence will mostly fail to place 50x. If exits stay ROE-based, the highest-confidence trades would systematically get worse R. The coded exits should be in price, ATR or R units so that leverage only changes size. Treat 50x at 15m/30m as unavailable unless the margin share or stop rule changes.

findings.claim: N10_HA_PSAR is the least-bad base among the 36 at 15m/30m. It is the only strategy that beat its same-side peers in all three runs at both timeframes. Its absolute expectancy is still about zero, and the 5-year result is clearly negative.
findings.evidence: N10_HA_PSAR@30m: every-signal +0.088R [-0.094,+0.253], n 49. Without the best 4h block: +0.046. Without the best day: +0.032. By run: v3a +0.21 (25), v3b +0.04 (13), v4 -0.13 (11); later -0.039R. Excess vs same-side peers +0.288R [0.115,0.440], BH q 0.005 (the only positive measure surviving BH). Account: +0.146R, n 16, PF 2.07, worst DD 16%. Side-flip -0.002R (n 22). 5-year: -0.132% per notional, t -19.3. 12.5 signals/day. N10_HA_PSAR@15m: -0.038R [-0.249,+0.170], n 109, later +0.066, same-side excess +0.20 [0.01,0.38], 24.7 signals/day. With 29 cells eligible, about 3.6 would be all-runs-positive on the relative measure by chance, so the run consistency alone is not strong. Source: cards_15_30.csv.
findings.implication: If the owners want one 15m/30m AI trader from the 36, N10_HA_PSAR (30m primary, 15m secondary) has the most support. It should be run as a pre-registered test of whether the AI's filtering adds R over the same signals, not as a proven earner.

findings.claim: S4_BB_BBP is the second candidate. At 15m it was strongly positive in v4 and has the largest favourable moves (MFE) of the 36, but it was negative in v3a and its 5-year result is negative.
findings.evidence: S4_BB_BBP@15m: every-signal +0.025R [-0.416,+0.616], n 95. By run: v3a -0.25 (56), v3b -0.14 (5), v4 +0.51 (34); later +0.42R. Account: +0.226R, n 22, PF 1.87, worst DD 15%. Mean MFE 1.43R; 19% of signals reach +1R. Side-flip +0.39R (n 39, p 0.10). 5-year: -0.152% per notional, t -38.7. 20.6 signals/day. S4_BB_BBP@30m (B): +0.110R, n 42, but later -0.04R.
findings.implication: S4_BB_BBP suits a trial of AI exit management, because its large MFE means exits matter. The positive v4 numbers could be the falling market and the quiet period. Keep it as a rule account in parallel so the AI's added value can be measured.

findings.claim: Account P&L is a poor guide. Accounts see only 15-35% of signals, and some top leaderboard cells are negative on every signal.
findings.evidence: S2_ST_ROC@15m: account +0.171R (n 39, PF 1.50), every-signal -0.198R (n 236). N07_ICHI_CMO@30m: BH-better than coin flips on account trades (q 0.014), but on only 8 trades against a 24-trade coin-flip pool. Its every-signal is +0.118R [-0.26,+0.49], n 14. Account vs every-signal mean R across 41 cells: Spearman 0.72, so they are related but not interchangeable. Source: cards_15_30.csv (acct_* vs es_* columns, cf_* from coinflip_pooled.csv).
findings.implication: Choose AI strategies, and promote or retire them, on every-signal replay statistics, not dashboard P&L.

findings.claim: These cells are clearly not worth a 15m/30m AI trader: negative live in every run or with a CI below zero, and negative in the 5-year backtest.
findings.implication: Do not spend Sonnet or Opus traders on these at 15m/30m. If they stay on, keep them as zero-cost rule accounts for monitoring only.

findings.claim: 16 of the 72 cells fire too rarely to support or validate a dedicated AI trader before 12/31.
findings.evidence: 8 cells never fired in the 4.6 days of every-signal data and fire 0-0.1 times/day in 5 years: N14_ICHI_RSI, N15_KC_AO, N21_ST_RSI_ADX, S1_EMA_RSI_CHOP, at both timeframes. 8 more fire under about 1/day live and in 5 years: N03_ADX_GC, N08_ICHI_WR, N11_BREAKAWAY, S5_DONCHIAN_MFI, at both timeframes. findings.claim: The house payoff structure needs a win rate of about 60% (15m) or 68% (30m) to break even, above the observed 53% and 59%. 30m is cheaper than 15m in R terms.
findings.evidence: Later runs: average stop-out -1.21R at 15m and -1.15R at 30m; average lock exit +0.82R and +0.53R. Breakeven win rate about 59.5% (15m) and 68.5% (30m); observed 53.1% and 59.3%. Median round-trip cost: 0.23R (15m) vs 0.16R (30m). 63% (15m) and 59% (30m) of signals reach +0.5R; 26.5% and 9.8% reach +1R. 25% of 15m stop-outs (13% at 30m) had first reached +0.5R. Sources: every_signal_rows_15_30.csv, pooled_15_30.csv.
findings.implication: For AI entries, 30m costs about 0.07R less per trade. Early take-profit can only reshape the payoff; it cannot create profit when gross is about zero. The AI's value has to come from which signals it takes.

findings.claim: The three runs are not like-for-like. v3a used tier-walk leverage, mostly 50x, which by itself lowers R, and v3b/v4 took place in a quiet, falling market. Differences between runs mix leverage, regime and noise.
findings.evidence: v3a 15m leverage mix 50:736 30:376 40:248 20:28, vs later 30:950 40:151 50:34. 50x vs the live rule costs -0.40R per signal at 15m (paired, n 176). Median 15m stop: 0.58% (v3a), 0.75% (v3b), 0.60% (v4). Long share at 15m in v4: 0.355. Sources: pooled_15_30.csv, levreplay_summary.csv.

Validation on 1,398 base rows: leverage equals the recorded fresh-account leverage in 100%. On 1,339 rows equal to real trades, the median difference between converted and actual R is 4e-16 (p95 3e-13). Unresolved: 545 shadows across all timeframes, for example 8 of 25 for N10_HA_PSAR@30m. Sources: v3a_every_signal.py, v3a_conversion_validation.csv.

limits: Every-signal data covers only 4.57 days: v3a 2.52 + v3b 0.62 + v4 1.43, in a quiet market (median 15m stop 0.6% of price) that fell during v3b and v4 (equal-weight -0.9% and -2.6%). Regime dependence cannot be judged; rising markets and high volatility are not represented.

Time clusters are few: a pooled cell has 15-31 four-hour clusters, and v3b alone has 5, so its intervals are too narrow to trust. The 4h-block bootstrap still treats blocks as independent, which understates uncertainty on trending days.

The runs differ in more than time. v3a used tier-walk leverage (mostly 50x, which costs R under the ROE ladder), v3b/v4 used quality_v1 (mostly 30x), and v3b has no skipped shadows (it uses the replay instead). Differences between runs mix leverage, market and noise.

545 v3a skipped shadows (all timeframes) were unresolved when the nightly job ran and are excluded; the bias sign is unknown. In the replay, the 10-12% of signals still open at the end are excluded from the main mean; marking them to the last close changes cell means by up to about 0.1R (columns *_incl_unres_mark).

The every-signal R measures the raw signal under house exits with one position per signal. It does not represent the planned AI behaviour (skipping, early take-profit or stop, near-signal entries, event reactions). The data cannot say whether an AI filter adds value; only a shadow comparison of the AI's picks against the same signals can.

The side-flip test assumes the opposite trade fills at the same quote (about 1bp in the flipped side's favour) and is confounded by market drift. The run-level same-side adjustment is a rough benchmark (it uses other strategies' timing), and a day-level version was rejected as unstable.

The 5-year reference is every signal under the OLD tier-walk leverage, example brackets and the $1,000 sizing equity, reported per notional. It shows the net loss is about the cost, but its per-cell spread is tiny (about +-0.02% per notional), so it cannot rank strategies within the 36.

The fixed-leverage replay uses brackets inferred from the export, not Binance's live table, so the bracket rejections at 50x for BCH/LTC may be overstated. Pairs exclude signals still open at the end, which tilts lower-leverage variants (longer holds) toward their faster exits.
The coin-flip bootstrap on account trades uses tiny pools (24 coin-flip trades at 30m). Its single BH-significant cell in this lens (N07_ICHI_CMO@30m) rests on 8 trades and is not trustworthy.

The tier rules were fixed before reading the results, but thresholds such as n>=20 are judgement calls (for example, DOGE@30m is C by rule but clearly negative). No cell can reach A while the 5-year result is negative for all of them.
lens:ours_15_30.report_section_md:
## Lens: our 36 strategies at 15m and 30m (the AI entry timeframes)

**Bottom line.** None of the 72 cells (36 strategies x 15m/30m) shows a positive edge that survives multiple testing, and the live results agree with the 5-year backtest. The 15m/30m signals have about zero gross directional edge, so each trade loses roughly its cost: about 0.23R at 15m and 0.16R at 30m. No cell earns tier A. Four 30m cells are B, all with confidence intervals that include zero, and two of those four are short-only or short-heavy strategies that benefited from the falling market. Only two cells come out as "least bad" bases for an AI test: **N10_HA_PSAR (30m, plus 15m)** and **S4_BB_BBP (15m/30m)**. Both are experiments, not verified non-losers.

### How the cards were built
- **Every signal per cell.**
  - v3a: entered trades (real R) plus the nightly skipped shadows. Shadow ROE was converted to R as ROE / (leverage x stop_frac), with the leverage and stop taken from the repo's own `PaperEngine` on a fresh $5,000 tier-walk account.
  - The conversion was checked on 1,398 base rows: leverage matched the recorded fresh-account leverage in 100% of rows. On the 1,339 rows that equal real trades, the median difference between converted and actual R is 4e-16.
  - v3b and v4: the pipeline replay of every SUBMITTED signal, status TRADED. UNRESOLVED signals are marked to the last close only as a sensitivity.
- **Uncertainty.** Bootstrap over time clusters (run x 4h block), resampled within each run, B = 10,000, with fixed seeds. 1h blocks are reported for reference. BH correction is applied over the cells tested.
- **Other columns.**
  - Side-flip excess comes from the pipeline. A drift-adjusted version subtracts the run x tf x side mean of the other strategies' flips.
  - Account statistics, the coin-flip bootstrap, 5-year net return per notional (with t and IS/CF), and signals per day live vs 5-year.
  - Cost share, MFE/MAE, and a fixed-leverage replay.
- **Tier rules (fixed before reading results).**
  - A: n>=30, mean>0, CI lower bound >0, positive in every run with n>=5 (at least 2 runs), side-flip excess >0, and the 5-year result not negative.
  - D: n>=20, mean<0, 5-year negative (t<-2), and either negative in every run with n>=5 or CI upper bound <0.
  - B: n>=20, mean>0, positive in most runs.
  - C: everything else.

### Results do not carry over between runs
- **Absolute results.** Every-signal mean R in v3a vs v3b+v4 (33 cells): Spearman -0.13 (p 0.47). All 4 cells that were positive in v3a were negative later. No cell is positive in all three runs; 11 are negative in all three.
- **Relative results.** The same-side-relative measure does not carry over either (Spearman -0.07 to +0.13).
- **Account P&L vs every signal.** Spearman 0.72 across cells, but they are not interchangeable. For example, S2_ST_ROC@15m has an account result of +0.17R (n 39) and an every-signal result of -0.20R (n 236).
- **Sample needed.** Days of every-signal data needed for a +-0.1R interval: about 11-14 for the most active cells (N04_ST_KLINGER@15m, N10_HA_PSAR@30m), 30-60 for typical cells, and more than 100 for S4_BB_BBP@15m.

### What this means for the AI-trader plan
1. **Do not expect any of the 36 at 15m/30m to supply an edge.** Each needs about +0.23R (15m) or +0.16R (30m) of value added by the AI just to break even. Treat any 15m/30m AI trader on these strategies as an experiment that must beat its own rule account on the same signals.
2. **If one or two such traders are funded,** use N10_HA_PSAR (30m entries, 15m secondary) and S4_BB_BBP (15m, to test AI exit management). Keep N13_3OUTSIDE@15m as a rule account to reconsider in November.
3. **Prefer 30m over 15m.** The cost share is 0.16R vs 0.23R, and win rates are similar.
4. **Make exits independent of leverage.** Define the coded exits in price, ATR or R units. With the current ROE ladder, raising leverage with confidence lowers R; and 50x at margin = leverage % can almost never be sized with a 2 ATR stop.
5. **Treat short-biased winners as regime bets.** N20_EMA9_CHOP and N24_DMI only look good because the market fell. Use them only with an explicit regime rule.
6. **Base the November promotion on every-signal replay with time-cluster CIs and criteria fixed in advance,** not on account P&L or leaderboard rank, which do not carry over between runs.
7. **Drop these from AI consideration:** the never-firing and under-1/day cells, and the BH-negative cells listed above.

Net mean R: 15m -0.172 [-0.180,-0.165] (n 1,113,807), 30m -0.126 [-0.133,-0.118], 1h -0.094 [-0.103,-0.086] (n 222,665), 4h -0.051 [-0.073,-0.029] (n 13,487). Gross R (cost added back) is ~0 at every timeframe: 15m -0.003, 30m -0.006, 1h -0.005 [-0.014,+0.003], 4h +0.011 [-0.011,+0.033]. Mean cost in R: 0.169 / 0.120 / 0.089 / 0.062. Live every-signal R, all 3 runs (live_cells.py -> tf_summary_live.csv; cluster = run x 4h block): 15m -0.235 [-0.373,-0.072] n 2529; 30m -0.205 [-0.293,-0.109] n 1117; 1h -0.091 [-0.219,+0.051] n 580 (by run: v3a -0.008, v3b -0.373, v4 -0.052); 4h +0.151 [-0.161,+0.456] n 55. findings.claim: Over 5 years, a 15m/30m signal that agrees with the 1h/4h state does slightly better than one that disagrees (+0.01 to +0.09R, same sign in IS and CF for 18 of 20 definitions). The agreeing signals still lose clearly, so watching 1h/4h trims losses but creates no edge.

limits: The live sample is 4.8 days in a quiet, mostly falling market. At 4h every cell has at most 5 every-signal outcomes, and the 4h total is 55 outcomes in 20 clusters, so per-cell live inference at 4h is impossible and at 1h very weak (n at most 59).

v3a has no live_bars. Its every-signal R combines exact entered-trade R with skipped-shadow R rebuilt from ROE using the tier-walk leverage. That leverage was reproduced for 95.7% of entered trades, and R is exact when it matches. 570 v3a shadows had no R (unresolved or not entered) and are excluded. The shadows used Binance final klines, while the entered trades used live fills.
Live replays still open at the run end are excluded from mean R (censoring). At 4h this is 30-60% of traded signals and biases the live 4h mean upward (censoring_check.csv).

The 5-year simulation is my copy of research/strategy_profiles/profiles.py::_scan, run on the signal-timeframe bars of the locked Binance signal cache. On a bar touching both stop and target it assumes the stop first. Funding is a constant 0.01%/8h, paid by both sides. Brackets are inferred from live trades. It uses only the quality_v1 'normal' group (30x, else 20x): strength-based 40/50x is not modeled. Every signal runs alone on $5,000; no account path, one-position limit or skipping. The cache ends 2026-09-30, so 5-year and live periods do not overlap. As a sanity check, my simulation agrees with the reference profiles (Spearman 0.87 over 55 cells).

The 5-year HTF states use the bot's own regime classifier (paperbot.context.regime) and simple momentum/EMA states on closed 1h/4h bars. same_pos uses the simulated 1h/4h exit of the latest sized signal, which only approximates a one-position rule account's real position. Live HTF states have warm-up gaps: in v3b (17h) the 4h momentum state was unavailable, and v3a prices are approximated from signal reference prices and fills.

Multiple testing: 20 pooled contrasts (10 definitions x 2 timeframes) per window are shown without correction; the per-strategy scan (505 cells with at least 30 per group) used BH, with 2 survivors and neither replicated in CF at t>2. The 72-cell grades use BH only for the 5-year gross test. The grading rule was written after seeing the per-timeframe aggregates but before reading per-cell results. N23_HA_ST 4h misses it by t 0.0004 and is flagged rather than regraded.

Cluster choices (run x 4h block live, UTC day for 5 years) may not capture all dependence, such as multi-day regimes. Live bootstrap CIs with 3-4 clusters, common at 4h and in v3b, are unreliable and should be read as descriptive.

Exit what-ifs (fy_exits.py) charge taker fee plus slippage on take-profit exits, which is conservative, and use an approximate liquidation price, which matters only on liquidation gaps. The 15m/30m rows use a 60k-signal sample per coin.

Nothing here measures what the AI's discretion (early take-profit, skips, near-signal entries, event reactions) would add. The data only show that the rule signals plus 1h/4h states carry no edge for the AI to amplify.
The DeepSeek ds200 1h/4h cells are outside this lens and were not graded.
lens:ours_1h_4h.report_section_md:
## Our 36 strategies at 1h and 4h: rule accounts and the AI's view timeframes

**Scope and method.** We built one evidence card per strategy x timeframe for 1h and 4h (72 cells; file `lens/ours_1h_4h/cards_1h_4h.csv`, 120 columns). Each card combines six sources:

- **Account trades per run:** v3a, v3b and v4 (`account_stats.csv`).
- **Every-signal outcomes:** every submitted signal, not only the trades an account took.
  - v3a: entered trades, plus nightly skipped shadows converted to R with the rebuilt tier-walk leverage.
  - v3b and v4: every submitted signal replayed alone on live_bars.
  - The 95% CI is a cluster bootstrap over run x 4-hour blocks.
- **Side-flip test:** the strategy's chosen side against the opposite side at the same moments.
- **The old 5-year reference profiles:** tier-walk leverage, results in ROE.
- **A new 5-year every-signal simulation under today's live rules** (`fy_sim.py`). It covers 36 strategies x 6 coins x 15m/30m/1h/4h from 2021-08 to 2026-09, 2.07M signals, with quality_v1 leverage (30x, else 20x), the 2 ATR stop, the ROE ladder and real costs. Results are in R, split into IS (2021-08..2024-06) and CF (2024-07..2026-09). Standard errors are clustered by UTC day.
- **Practical fields:** signals per day, sizing rejections per coin, and cost as a share of the stop.

Two further 5-year studies test whether 15m/30m signals do better when they agree with the 1h/4h state, and how exit and leverage custom values change results. The same agreement test was then run on the three live runs as an out-of-sample check.

### 1. Is the edge at 1h/4h? No. The higher timeframes only lose less.

| tf | live every-signal mean R [95% CI] (n) | live accounts mean R (n) | 5-year net R [95% CI] | 5-year gross R [95% CI] | 5-year cost in R | live median cost in R |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15m | -0.235 [-0.373, -0.072] (2,529) | -0.190 (630) | -0.172 [-0.180, -0.165] | -0.003 [-0.009, +0.004] | 0.169 | 0.224 |
| 30m | -0.205 [-0.293, -0.109] (1,117) | -0.152 (378) | -0.126 [-0.133, -0.118] | -0.006 [-0.013, +0.001] | 0.120 | 0.158 |
| 1h | -0.091 [-0.219, +0.051] (580) | -0.073 (212) | -0.094 [-0.103, -0.086] | -0.005 [-0.014, +0.003] | 0.089 | 0.113 |
| 4h | +0.151 [-0.161, +0.456] (55) | +0.144 (31) | -0.051 [-0.073, -0.029] | +0.011 [-0.011, +0.033] | 0.062 | 0.070 |

Sources: `tf_summary_live.csv`, `tf_summary_5y.csv`, rb_analyze `kind_tf_summary` and `cost_by_tf`.

- **Gross R is zero at every timeframe.** The ranking 15m < 30m < 1h < 4h is the ranking of cost as a share of the stop. The signals are no better at higher timeframes.
- **The live 1h figure is not stable across runs:** v3a -0.008, v3b -0.373, v4 -0.052.
- **The live 4h mean is inflated by censoring** (trades still open at run end are left out). In v4, 26 traded signals average +0.198, but 11 more were still open at the end, marked at -0.207. Including them gives +0.078. In v3b, +0.301 becomes -0.008.
- **Direction skill is absent.** The side-flip test against a coin flip gives 1h excess -0.024R (338 pairs, p 0.64) and 4h +0.127R (28 pairs, 9 clusters, p 0.36). Of 20 testable cells, one has raw p < 0.05: N20_EMA9_CHOP 1h, BH q 0.52.

### 2. Tradability: 4h is mostly blocked, and 20-50x does not fit 1h/4h

Share of signals whose 2 ATR stop sits at least 1 ATR inside liquidation (`lev_feasibility.csv`):

| tf | 5y >=50x | 5y >=40x | 5y >=30x | 5y >=20x | live >=50x | live >=40x | live >=30x | live >=20x |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15m | 7.4% | 35.7% | 81.1% | 97.6% | 28.3% | 74.6% | 99.0% | 100% |
| 30m | 2.2% | 13.5% | 56.7% | 92.4% | 11.1% | 41.9% | 93.3% | 100% |
| 1h | 0.4% | 3.6% | 26.9% | 77.4% | 1.7% | 9.2% | 68.2% | 98.6% |
| 4h | 0% | 0% | 1.1% | 19.3% | 0% | 0% | 2.8% | 46.1% |

- **Live 4h rejections by coin.** In v3b and v4, all 39 BCH/DOGE/LTC 4h signals were rejected for "stop too close to liquidation". The 28 traded 4h signals were BTC 3, ETH 12 and SOL 13, all at 20x.
- **Five-year 4h sizable share at 20x by coin:** BTC 55%, ETH 26%, SOL 4%, DOGE 8%, LTC 13%, BCH 9%.
- **Account-level rejections for our 36:** v3a 4h 35, v3a 1h 8, v3b 4h 8, v4 4h 12.
- **Volume:** across all 36 strategies, 5 years produced 118 sized 1h signals and 7.2 sized 4h signals per day.
- **Implication for the AI design:** with a 2 ATR code stop, "20-50x by confidence" is mostly cut down by sizing. At 15m, 50x fits 7% of signals (5-year) to 28% (this quiet market). At 1h/4h nothing above 30x/20x fits.

### 3. Grades for the 72 cells

| grade | rule | 1h | 4h |

| A | 5-year net t >= 2 in IS and CF and live every-signal CI > 0 | 0 | 0 |

| C | no directional edge; net is about minus the cost | 26 | 21 |
| D | 5-year net t <= -2 with gross <= -0.02, or live CI < 0 | 6 | 2 |
| U | < 100 sized 5-year signals and < 10 live outcomes | 4 | 13 |

Negative (D) cells:
- DOGE 1h and N04_ST_KLINGER 1h, on the live every-signal CI. N04_ST_KLINGER 1h: -0.233 [-0.41, -0.04], n 57.
- N17_KC_RSI at 1h and 4h. This mean-reversion strategy loses before costs: gross -0.048 (t -4.0) at 1h and -0.088 (t -2.9) at 4h, in both halves.
- N16_BBRSI 1h, S3_CMO_SANDWICH 1h, S5_DONCHIAN_MFI 1h and OBV_B 4h.

Silent cells: N14_ICHI_RSI, N15_KC_AO, N21_ST_RSI_ADX and S1_EMA_RSI_CHOP have almost no 1h/4h signals in 5 years.

### 4. Which strategies are better on 1h/4h than on 15m/30m?

- **5 years, net:** 44 of 66 strategy comparisons are significantly better at the higher timeframe after BH (`fy_tfcompare.csv`). This is the cost effect.
- **5 years, gross (cost added back):** only N23_HA_ST 4h is better: +0.086R against its pooled 15m/30m, t 3.86, BH q 0.007, IS +0.075, CF +0.095.
  - Runner-up: N22_VORTEX_PSAR 4h, +0.062 (t 2.35, q 0.43).
  - Worse at higher timeframes before costs: N17_KC_RSI, 1h -0.022 (t -2.34) and 4h -0.062 (t -2.08).
- **Live:** 9 of 35 cells show a positive higher-minus-lower difference with CI > 0, but 8 of them rest on 3-4 clusters and n <= 5 at the higher timeframe. The only well-clustered case is N25_DST_CCI 1h: -0.038 (n 31) against 15m -0.528 (n 116) and 30m -0.337 (n 55), consistent with lower cost. It is not corrected for multiple testing.

### 5. Does a 15m/30m signal do better when it agrees with 1h/4h? Slightly, and it still loses

| same strategy 1h position open | +0.030 (1.7) / +0.025 (1.4) | +0.032 (1.8) / +0.018 (0.9) | **-0.057 (-5.5) / -0.036 (-3.4)** |
| same strategy 4h position open | +0.053 (1.4) / +0.092 (2.6) | +0.040 (1.0) / +0.037 (0.9) | **-0.182 (-6.1) / -0.078 (-3.1)** |

- **Agreement helps a little and consistently.** 18 of 20 IS/CF pairs have the same sign. The size is +0.01 to +0.09R, and no definition reaches t > 2 in both halves.
- **The agree groups still lose.** At 15m, mean R when agreeing with the 4h regime is -0.110 (IS) and -0.100 (CF), and only about 3% of signals have a trend label at all. At 15m, agreeing with the same strategy's 4h signal gives -0.153 / -0.159.
- **The best combined case still loses.** Signals where at least 3 of 5 HTF states agree (exploratory score, 15% of signals; `fy_htf_score_buckets.csv`) score -0.132 / -0.149 at 15m and -0.111 / -0.096 at 30m.
- **Piling on is worse than a clean entry.** A same-direction 1h/4h position already open is worse than no HTF position, by -0.04 to -0.18R with t from -2.3 to -6.7, in both halves.
- **No strategy-specific HTF effect holds up.** With at least 30 signals in both the agree and against groups, 505 strategy x timeframe x definition cells were tested. BH leaves 2 in IS, and neither replicates in CF at t > 2. IS-versus-CF correlations of the per-strategy effects range from -0.66 to +0.36 (`fy_htf_by_strategy_min30.csv`).

**Live check (out of sample).** Sources: `live_htf_contrasts.csv` and `live_htf_groups.csv`.

| same strategy 1h signal | +0.23 [+0.005, +0.50] | -0.165 (576) | -0.372 (293) | +0.48 | +0.15 | +0.13 |

- **The signs mostly match the 5-year result, but the sizes are 5-20x larger.** The estimates flip between runs: the same-strategy 4h signal is negative in v3b and v4.
- **The agree groups are about zero or below in every run.** The one exception is 4h momentum in v4 (+0.303, n 376), which was 33% long in a falling market.
- **Conclusion:** live data cannot confirm or refute an effect of about 0.02R.

### 6. Custom values and exits at 1h/4h (5 years, paired on the same signals)

Each cell is the change in mean R versus base, with t in brackets. Source: `fy_exits.csv`; base reproduces fy_sim for 100% of signals.

| tf | lev10 | lock20 | lock30 | ladder in R units | tp1R | tp2R | time stop (64 bars) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1h | +0.011 (2.3) | +0.003 (1.2) | +0.006 (1.4) | +0.002 (0.8) | -0.002 (-0.5) | +0.006 (0.6) | +0.000 |
| 4h | +0.009 (1.0) | +0.001 (0.1) | -0.004 (-0.4) | +0.006 (0.6) | -0.014 (-1.0) | +0.030 (1.1) | 0 |

- **No custom value creates an edge.** Base mean R is -0.094 at 1h and -0.051 at 4h, and the changes above are a few hundredths of R at most.
- **The nightly live what-ifs overstate the gains.** At 1h they showed lev10 +0.216R and lock30 +0.179R, built on pairs that are partly unresolved and biased. Five years support only about +0.01R from 10x leverage, which puts the ROE ladder further away in price.

### 7. What this means for the AI-trader plan

1. **Do not give any 1h/4h strategy an AI slot because of 1h/4h results.** No cell shows a live or 5-year edge. 1h/4h only lose less, because cost takes less of the stop.
2. **The AI's 1h/4h view is at best a small loss reducer.**
   - Vetoing entries against the 1h/4h state is worth about +0.02 to +0.08R relative, which is far below the 0.12-0.17R cost of 15m/30m.
   - Treating an already-open same-direction 1h/4h rule position as confirmation is harmful: it marks a late entry.
3. **Fix leverage by timeframe and by the stop rule before going live.**
   - 50x with a 2 ATR stop fits only 7-28% of 15m signals and almost no 30m/1h/4h signals.
   - 4h rule accounts are BTC/ETH accounts in practice.
4. **Keep 1h/4h as cost-free rule accounts. Watch one line: N23_HA_ST 4h.** It has a gross +0.09R that survives BH in both halves, but net is about 0, it trades about 0.7 times a day, and live n is 4.
   - N22_VORTEX_PSAR 4h is the runner-up.
   - N17_KC_RSI, N04_ST_KLINGER 1h and the other D cells can be ignored.
5. **Nothing at 1h/4h can be verified by 12/31.** Detecting ±0.05R needs about 1,500-1,700 trades per cell. November promotions from 1h/4h accounts would rest on noise.

findings.claim: No DeepSeek definition earns a dedicated AI trader at 15m or 30m. Nothing survives multiple testing in the live every-signal replay, and every 15m/30m cell is negative after costs in the 5-year test.
findings.evidence: Live (v4, 1.50 days, out/cards_deepseek.csv from cards.py + grade.py): 61 testable cells (>=10 replayed trades and >=8 one-hour clusters; 31 at 15m, 20 at 30m, 10 at 1h). 0 of them have BH q<=0.10 for mean R>0. The smallest raw one-sided cluster-t p is 0.137 (F16_FIB500@15m, +0.29R, n13). 5-year (research/deepseek200/out/results.csv): all 88 definition x tf cells at 15m and 30m have negative pooled net mean (periods 1+2) under both PREREG exits. Best is -0.083%/trade at 15m and -0.076% at 30m, both F15_OPEN0930. 0/342 candidates. Grades over the 88 15m/30m cards: A 0, W 1 (F9_IFVG@15m), C 49, D 13, X 16, N 9.
findings.implication: Do not use AI-trader budget on DeepSeek definitions as 12/31 candidates. Keep all 44 as cost-free rule accounts. If DeepSeek gets any AI slot, it is an exploratory slot outside the judged set (see DS14).

findings.claim: The v4 live window is essentially one directional move, so per-definition live results mostly measure how short-heavy a definition was during the 10/07 sell-off, not skill.
findings.evidence: ds200 replay (replay_signals.csv; split at the run midpoint 10/06 21:37 KST). 15m first half: longs -0.37R (n296), shorts -0.20R (n350). Second half: longs -0.86R (n234), shorts +1.27R (n240). 30m second half: longs -0.90R, shorts +0.91R. Across the 51 testable 15m/30m cells, long share vs mean R has Spearman -0.45 (p 0.0008). Cell mean R in the first half vs the second half has Spearman -0.59 at 15m (n31, p<0.001), -0.41 at 30m (n20, p 0.07) and -0.55 over all testable cells (n59) (out/diagnostics.csv, halves.csv). Equal-weight 6 coins fell 2.6% in v4 (market_backdrop.csv).
findings.implication: Never rank DeepSeek (or any) strategies for AI slots on the v4 leaderboard. Use side-balanced R and R vs same-moment peers. The AI's direction calls in its first weeks will be scored in whatever regime comes next, and a single trend can flip any ranking.

findings.claim: Costs, not signal direction, decide the 15m result. ds200 15m signals were gross-positive in this window but lost after fees, funding and slippage. In the 5-year, gross is already negative at every timeframe.
findings.evidence: tf_summary_ds.csv (every replayed signal; cluster-t 95% CI with one-hour clusters). 15m: n1120, mean -0.065R [-0.21,+0.08], gross +0.18R, fees+funding 0.177R, slippage 0.071R, median stop 0.60% of price. 30m: n586, -0.132R [-0.26,-0.01], gross +0.04R, costs 0.12+0.05R. 1h: n330, -0.112R [-0.23,+0.00]. Net per trade on notional: 15m -0.061%, 30m -0.115%, 1h -0.150%, 4h -0.233%. That is the same order as the 5-year net (15m -0.151% period 1 / -0.141% period 2, 30m -0.160/-0.149). 5-year gross before costs: 15m -0.047%, 30m -0.053%. At 30x, a 0.14% round trip is about 4.2% ROE per trade.
findings.implication: A DeepSeek AI trader at 15m must add about +0.25R per trade over the rule just to break even (+0.17R at 30m). Exits, skipping and cheaper entries would have to create that. Signal choice alone has never shown it.

findings.claim: The one-position account results (the dashboard leaderboard) are a poor estimate even of the window's own every-signal result.
findings.evidence: 141 ds200 accounts traded (median 3 trades, max 12). 52 were profitable, and 27 of those turn negative without their best trade (luck_concentration.csv). Account total: 563 trades, -$37,091, mean R -0.201. Examples: F12_MSS@15m is the 3rd-best account (+$1,229 on 4 trades) but its every-signal replay is -0.10R (n24). F3_HHHL@15m account is -$1,715 (6 trades, -1.20R) but its replay is +0.20R (n41). Spearman of account mean R vs replay mean R: 0.42 at 15m, 0.65 at 30m (diagnostics.csv).
findings.implication: Judge strategies on every-signal replays or shadow books, never on single-position account PnL. The AI trader is also one-position, so its realized R will be even noisier than the replay.

findings.claim: DeepSeek direction skill against a coin flip at the same moments is weak, and about a third of it is market drift.
findings.evidence: Pipeline side-flip (coinflip_sideflip.csv): ds200 15m excess +0.073R (1107 pairs, 35 clusters, cluster p 0.024); 30m -0.028R; all timeframes +0.032R (p 0.14); no definition x tf cell significant after BH. Drift-neutral version (equal-weight long and short excess, sideflip_drift.py -> out/sideflip_drift.csv): 15m +0.049R (p 0.08), 30m -0.023R (p 0.68), all +0.028R (p 0.17). For comparison, the core 36 at 15m: +0.089R raw but -0.084R drift-neutral. The 5-year gross per trade is negative, so the 5-year shows no direction skill either.
findings.implication: There is no reliable directional edge for an AI to amplify. The 15m drift-neutral +0.05R (p 0.08, one of 8 kind x tf looks) is a reason to keep recording, not a reason to choose.

findings.claim: The 44 definitions are about 35 distinct streams. Nine definitions duplicate or nest inside a parent, and two definitions emit the same stream on several timeframes.
findings.evidence: dup_pairs_ds.csv (signal level: bar_close, coin, side). F5_BOX_HTF = F5_BOX (identical 10/10 at 15m, 4/4 at 30m). F13_RAID_PD is inside F11_RAID (36/38 at 15m, identical at 1h and 4h). F11_TSOUP: 22 of 25 signals at 15m are also F11_RAID signals. F17_Z_HL is inside F17_Z (47/50 at 15m, identical at 1h and 4h). F12_MSS_DISP is inside F12_MSS (12/12 at 15m). F13_FVG_PD and F10_M2022 are inside F9_FVG. F16_FIB618 is inside F10_OTE (14/14 at 15m, identical at 4h). 75% of F7_RF_ONLY signals are F7_RF_TRIPLE signals. F15_OPEN0000 emits one identical stream at 15m/30m/1h (12/12), and F15_OPEN0930 is identical at 15m/30m; only the ATR stop differs. The F1 divergences overlap 60-80%. In the 5-year, children are not reliably better than parents (e.g. F12_MSS_DISP 15m -0.126% vs F12_MSS -0.160%; F17_Z_HL -0.142% vs F17_Z -0.130%).
findings.implication: Keep the parent: F5_BOX, F11_RAID, F17_Z, F12_MSS, F9_FVG, F10_OTE, F7_RF_TRIPLE, F15_OPEN0000@15m, F15_OPEN0930@15m. Use the child filters (HTF ADX, premium/discount, half-life, displacement) as context the AI sees, not as separate traders. Count families, not definitions, when correcting for multiple testing.

findings.claim: The 5-year stage-1 passers are named differently in RESULTS_DEEPSEEK200.md and results.csv. This analysis reports both and does not resolve it. Every disputed row is a 4h row outside the AI's 15m/30m entry timeframes.
findings.evidence: results.csv flags stage1=True on 4h F5_BOX X2_SL15_TP3 (periods 1/2/3: +0.057/-0.413/+0.859%, n 165/160/91) and 4h F13_FVG_PD X5_TRAIL2 (+0.202/-0.532/+0.617%, n 257/231/121). per_family.csv agrees (F5 1, F13 1). The md says the two stage-1 passers were 4h F1_RSI_DIV X2 (+0.045/+0.183/+0.456%, n 674/508/246) and 4h F10_M2022 X5 (+0.058/+0.155/+0.027%, n 116/91/41). In results.csv those two rows carry all3_positive=True and stage1=False, and near_miss.csv lists them as all_three_periods_positive. The row fields: F1_RSI_DIV period-1 second half -0.330%; F10_M2022 2 of 6 coins positive. Both versions agree on stage 2 = 0, BH = 0 and candidates = 0. Live v4: F5_BOX@4h 0 signals, F13_FVG_PD@4h 1 trade +0.20R, F1_RSI_DIV@4h 1 trade -1.05R, F10_M2022@4h 0 signals.
findings.implication: Whichever document is right, no candidate exists and nothing changes for 15m/30m AI selection. Fix the wording in the md before anyone cites it. AIBOT_DESIGN_KO_v2 item 6 already flags the mismatch.

findings.claim: Between-definition differences in the 5-year do not persist across periods, so 'least-bad in the 5-year' is also a weak selector.
findings.evidence: diagnostics.csv: Spearman of period-1 vs period-2 net mean across the 44 definitions (exit picked on period 1): 15m -0.14 (p 0.36), 30m -0.15 (p 0.34), 1h +0.15, 4h -0.03. Period 1 vs period 3: +0.12 / +0.09 / +0.07 / -0.04. Live replay mean R vs 5-year rank: 15m +0.02 (p 0.90), 30m +0.33 (p 0.15). The 15m 5-year range across definitions is only -0.189% to -0.083% per trade.
findings.implication: Choosing DeepSeek AI traders by 5-year rank is close to random. If slots are given, choose them by families, signal frequency (learning value) and non-duplication, and say openly that the choice is exploratory.

findings.claim: The only DeepSeek cells with a positive 5-year net mean are 9 low-frequency 1h/4h cells, mostly the F1 divergence family at 4h. None passes the gates, and they are not AI-entry timeframes.
findings.evidence: cards_deepseek.csv y_best_mean12_pct>0: F4_PULL_RSI@4h +0.334%/trade (period-1 n 80), F1_PVT_DIV@4h +0.265%, F5_BOX_RSI@1h +0.139%, F1_RSI_DIV@4h +0.104% (all 3 periods positive under X2), F10_M2022@4h +0.101% (all 3 positive under X5), F1_MOM_DIV@4h +0.088%, F12_MSS_DISP@4h +0.084%, F4_PULL@4h +0.031%, F5_BOX@1h +0.010%. findings.claim: F4_PULL is the only definition that is significantly negative after BH, at 15m and 30m. At 30m that is mostly direction: all 20 trades were longs during the decline.
findings.evidence: F4_PULL@15m -0.59R (n52, 24 clusters, CI [-0.95,-0.23], BH q(mean<0) 0.035); both sides were negative (longs -0.89, shorts -0.24, side-balanced -0.56, vs peers -0.20). F4_PULL@30m -1.00R (n20, CI [-1.26,-0.74], q 0.0001), 20/20 long. F4_PULL@1h -0.47R (n17, all long). Family F4 at 30m (unique signals) -0.48R [-0.90,-0.05]. 5-year F4_PULL: 15m -0.129%, 30m -0.172%, 4h +0.031%.

findings.claim: Leverage under the house rules: 40-50x is mostly not executable for DeepSeek signals. With the ROE-based ladder, lower leverage (a later first lock) gave better R in this window, on both sides. Leverage changes the exit, not only the size.
findings.evidence: levreplay.py (every ds200 signal at fixed L with margin = L% through the repo engine; parity at 30x is exact on 1,996 signals) -> lev_replay_summary.csv. Entered share at 15m: 10-30x 100%, 40x 90%, 50x 21%. At 30m: 30x 99.7%, 40x 40%, 50x 0%. At 1h: 30x 83%, 40x+ 0%. At 50x the rejections cite loss above 15% of equity (885), bracket (753) and liquidation buffer (405). Mean R including marked open trades: 15m 10x +0.029, 20x -0.073, 30x -0.077, 40x -0.200 (on its 90%). 30m 10x -0.041, 20x -0.123, 30x -0.140, 40x -0.227. Side split at 15m, 10x vs 30x: longs -0.89 vs -0.55, shorts +0.84 vs +0.35; side-balanced 10x is still +0.08R better (30m +0.10R). Mechanism: the first lock triggers at +12% ROE, i.e. 0.12/L of price. At 30x that is about 0.9R at 15m. The nightly d3 lev10 what-if shows the opposite sign (-0.23R at 15m); it drops 75 slow unresolved ds200 rows. On account-entered, resolved-only pairs the replay gives +0.002R at 15m.
findings.implication: Define the AI's exits in price/R, as design 3-4/4-1 intends, not in ROE. Otherwise a 'confidence -> 50x' rule silently tightens the take-profit. Under margin = leverage%, 50x cannot take most 15m and no 30m DeepSeek signals. Prefer the design's risk-per-stop sizing (4-3), where leverage is an output. Whether a later lock really helps is regime-dependent and was not tested out of sample.

findings.claim: Near-signal limit entries do not fix the cost problem. Fills are adversely selected.
findings.evidence: d3 limit what-if (0.25 ATR better, one bar; 10/06 signals only) matched to the replay (d3check.py -> d3_checks_ds_limitR.csv). Fill rate 65% at 15m and 58% at 30m. Filled signals were the losers at market (-0.38R / -0.40R), and the unfilled ones ran away (+0.26R / +0.30R). Per signal, limit vs market: 15m -0.141 vs -0.156R (+0.015R), 30m -0.096 vs -0.104R (+0.008R). Separately, the d3 skipped shadows equal the replay exactly on 1,016 matched ds200 signals (abs diff 0), so they are not independent evidence.
findings.implication: Do not count on AI 'near-signal' or limit entries to close the 0.17-0.25R cost gap. Maker fees (about 0.02%) would help more than price improvement. Measure this as its own shadow before trusting it.

findings.claim: Statistical power: one DeepSeek cell needs months to show a realistic edge. By the November promotion only edges of about 0.2R or more could be seen, before multiple-testing correction.
findings.evidence: Per-trade sd of R: 1.41 at 15m, 1.00 at 30m. Median cell cluster SE 0.27R / 0.25R (design effect 1.15 / 1.44). Median MDE80 about 0.74R / 0.71R in this window. Detecting +0.1R at 80% power needs about 1,400 signals at 15m (~78 days at the median cell's 18 signals/day) and about 900 at 30m (~79 days). Detecting +0.2R needs about 350 / 220 signals (~20 days). The AI trader takes one position at a time, so it sees far fewer trades than signals.
findings.implication: With about 30 traders judged at once, only large AI value-added (well above +0.2R per trade) can be confirmed by 12/31. Plan the AI evaluation on shadow every-signal books plus R-based paired comparisons (AI vs the rule on the same signals), not on account PnL.

findings.claim: If the owners still want DeepSeek exposure in the AI cohort, at most 1-2 exploratory family traders are defensible, and none as a 12/31 candidate.
findings.evidence: Family x tf (unique signals, family_tf.csv / family_verdict.csv). F6 VWAP: 15m +0.08R (n114, CI [-0.45,+0.61]), ~76 unique signals/day. Its 5-year is the least negative among frequent families: VWAP_CROSS ranks 4/44 at 15m (-0.114%) and 2/44 at 30m (-0.096%), and F6_VWAP_CROSS@1h is the only W outside 15m (+0.15R, n34). F9 FVG/OB: 15m -0.01R (n108); F9_IFVG@15m is the only W at 15m (+0.06R, n26, side-balanced +0.09, vs peers +0.15, 5-year rank 8/44). F1 divergence: 15m +0.24R (n38, CI [-0.44,+0.93], drift-neutral side-flip +0.28, p 0.19), but its 15m 5-year ranks are poor (30, 36 and 5 of 44) and its only 5-year support is at 4h. Avoid F4, F11/F13 raid, F14_SMT (15m -0.14R n112; 30m -0.29R n39), F16, F17 and F8.
findings.implication: Recommended: zero DeepSeek AI traders in the judged cohort. If one or two exploratory slots are wanted, use one trader per family (F6 VWAP, then F9 FVG), deduplicated, Sonnet only, outside the 12/31 set. Their purpose is to learn whether AI exits and skipping can recover the 0.2R cost gap, not to find the strategy to take to real money.

limits: One run, one regime: ds200 exists only in v4 (1.50 days, 10/06 03:35 to 10/07 15:40 KST), a falling market (6-coin equal weight -2.6%), with one sell-off doing most of the work. There is no v3a/v3b out-of-sample run for DeepSeek. The within-run halves anti-correlate (Spearman -0.59 at 15m), so the window cannot rank definitions.

Per-cell samples are tiny: median 3 account trades and 9-25 replayed signals for most 15m/30m cells. The median minimum detectable effect at 80% power is about 0.7R per cell, and the cluster counts (one-hour blocks, 2-36 per cell) are small. Cluster-t intervals with few clusters are unreliable, and some cells (F11_PO3@1h, F15 daily signals) show artificially tight CIs.

Primary replay means use resolved trades only. 140 of 2,286 ds200 signals were still open at the end and are only in the marked sensitivity (rp_mean_R_incl_marked). 59 4h signals were rejected by sizing at 20x.

The nightly d3 skipped shadows equal the replay exactly on 1,016 matched signals, so they are not independent evidence. The d3 per-trade variants (lev/lock/tp) pair only resolved rows within the night's horizon and are biased. Their lev10 sign at 15m contradicts the full replay.

The 5-year reference uses the PREREG exits (X5_TRAIL2 / X2_SL15_TP3), unlevered % per trade, next-bar-open entry, and one position per (config, coin). The live accounts use house exits (2 ATR stop + ROE ladder at 30x/20x). Comparisons are therefore only in % per trade on notional. 5-year per_day counts trades, not signals.
The RESULTS_DEEPSEEK200.md vs results.csv stage-1 disagreement is reported, not resolved. Either way stage 2 = 0 and candidates = 0.

The grade rubric (testable = n>=10 and >=8 clusters; W needs side-balanced, ex-best, vs-peers >0 and 5-year >= tf median; D = BH-negative or negative live with a worst-third 5-year) was fixed after seeing the overall picture and is not pre-registered. It is mechanical, but its thresholds are judgment calls. No threshold variant produces a BH-positive cell.
Side-balanced R needs >=3 trades per side and is missing for many cells. R vs peers uses other core-36 + ds200 signals in the same tf/side/4h block, which is not a random benchmark.

The leverage replay uses margin = leverage %, the house sizing limits (15% max loss at stop, 1 ATR liquidation buffer) and the pipeline's inferred brackets and funding. The AI design's 4-3 risk-per-stop sizing would admit different signals. The 'later lock is better' result comes from one trending window and is untested elsewhere.

Nothing here measures what an AI trader adds (skipping, early exits, switching, near-signal entries). Rule-bot data can only bound what the AI must add (about +0.25R/trade at 15m, +0.17R at 30m, to cover costs).

FORWARD_PREREG (DeepSeek shadow forward test, PREREG exits, no performance looks before 11/04) was not touched. Only the house-exit paper accounts were analysed. Choosing AI traders from these data is an extra look that the forward test's N=498 does not count.
The F14_SMT live results cover 5 coins (BTC is only the reference). The F15 daily-session definitions produce one decision per coin per day, so 1.5 days gives 1-2 independent events.
lens:deepseek.report_section_md:
## DeepSeek 44 definitions (ds200, paper v4): evidence cards and AI-trader verdict

**Question.** Which of the 44 DeepSeek definitions (171 accounts at 15m/30m/1h/4h; the F15 ET-session definitions run only at 15m/30m/1h) deserve a dedicated AI trader that enters on 15m/30m signals?

**Answer.** None, on the evidence. Keep all 44 as cost-free rule accounts. If the owners want DeepSeek represented anyway, give at most one or two exploratory family traders (F6 VWAP, then F9 FVG), outside the 12/31 candidate set.

### Data and method
- **Accounts.** v4 ds200 trades: `trades_enriched.csv` / `account_stats.csv`. 563 trades, -$37,091, mean R -0.201. 141 of 171 accounts traded; 20 had no signal; 7 had positions still open at the end. Median 3 trades per account.
- **Every-signal replay.** All 2,286 SUBMITTED ds200 signals were run alone through the repo engine on `live_bars` (`replay_signals.csv`): 2,087 traded, 140 still open (marked to the last close in a sensitivity), 59 rejected by sizing (all 4h). The replay matches the real trades exactly.
- **Uncertainty.** Cluster-robust t intervals with G-1 df. Clusters are the signal bar floored to max(tf, 1h), with 4h blocks as a sensitivity. BH at 10% runs over the 61 *testable* cells (>=10 replayed trades and >=8 clusters).
- **Direction checks.** Side-balanced R is the mean of the long and short means. R vs peers is R minus the mean R of other strategies' signals with the same tf, side and 4h block. The half split is at the run midpoint, 10/06 21:37 KST.
- **Side-flip.** From the pipeline, plus a drift-neutral version (`sideflip_drift.py`).
- **5-year.** `research/deepseek200/out/results.csv`: both PREREG exits, periods 1/2/3, gross, stage flags. The live signal code hash (lib_c.py 3210c602...) equals the 5-year code hash.
- **Duplicates.** Signal-level overlap of every definition pair at the same tf, and the same definition across tfs (`dup_pairs_ds.csv`).

### 2. Why the per-definition live ranking cannot be used
The v4 window is one directional move.

| ds200 replay, mean R (n) | first half: longs | first half: shorts | second half: longs | second half: shorts |

| 15m | -0.37 (296) | -0.20 (350) | -0.86 (234) | **+1.27 (240)** |

- **Long share explains the result.** Across the 51 testable 15m/30m cells, long share vs mean R has Spearman -0.45 (p 0.0008).

### 7. Exits and leverage (house rules)
| tf | entered share at 10/20/30/40/50x | mean R at 10x / 20x / 30x / 40x (incl. marked) | 10x vs 30x, longs | 10x vs 30x, shorts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15m | 100/100/100/90/21% | +0.03 / -0.07 / -0.08 / -0.20 | -0.89 vs -0.55 | +0.84 vs +0.35 |
| 30m | 100/100/99.7/40/0% | -0.04 / -0.12 / -0.14 / -0.23 | -0.82 vs -0.45 | +0.74 vs +0.17 |
| 1h | 100/100/83/0/0% | +0.02 / -0.08 / -0.14 / n/a | | |

- **Mechanism.** The ROE ladder's first lock triggers at +12% ROE, which is 0.12/L of price: about 0.9R at 15m at 30x, about 2.2R at 10x. Higher leverage therefore means an earlier profit lock. In this trending window a later lock was better, also side-balanced (+0.08R at 15m, +0.10R at 30m).
- **Feasibility.** With margin = leverage %, 50x cannot take most 15m signals or any 30m DeepSeek signal (rejections: loss above 15% of equity, bracket, liquidation buffer).
- **Nightly d3 what-ifs** (biased, resolved pairs only): tp1R +0.08R and stopw3 +0.05R at 15m; lock30 -0.17R; tp2R -0.08R; tp3R -0.26R.
- **Limit entry** (0.25 ATR, 10/06 only): fills 65% / 58%. Fills are the would-be losers and misses the runaway winners. Net per signal: +0.015R at 15m, +0.008R at 30m.

### 8. What this means for the AI plan
1. **No DeepSeek AI trader in the judged cohort.** The AI would need to add about +0.25R/trade at 15m (+0.17R at 30m) just to cover costs. No rule-level evidence (live replay, side-flip, 5-year) shows a starting edge.
2. **If there is an exploratory slot**, use one family trader with deduplicated streams, Sonnet only: F6 VWAP first, then F9 FVG/IFVG/OB/Breaker. Never F4, the F11/F13 raids, F14_SMT, F16 or F17.
3. **Keep the 4h F1 divergence group, F4_PULL_RSI@4h, F10_M2022@4h and F5_BOX_RSI@1h as rule accounts.** They are the only places the 5-year leaves room, and they fire 0 to 0.7 times per day.
4. **Exits in price/R, not ROE.** Confidence should scale risk per stop (design 4-3), not leverage. Otherwise "50x when confident" silently means "take profit sooner", and most 15m/30m signals cannot be sized at 50x anyway.
5. **Evaluate on every-signal shadow books and paired AI-vs-rule R on the same signals.** At this noise level (sd 1.0-1.4R per trade, median per-cell MDE about 0.7R now), +0.1R per cell needs about 900-1,400 signals (about 80 days). Only effects of about 0.2R or more can be seen by the November promotion.

### What the data cannot tell
Whether any definition has an edge in another regime. Whether AI discretion adds value. Whether the "later lock" effect generalises. Which stage-1 list in the 5-year documents is the intended one.

findings.claim: The house exit is not the main loss source at 15m/30m: on every submitted signal the gross R is about zero and the round-trip cost explains all of the 15m loss and about 80% of the 30m loss. Exits only reshape the distribution: across 34 exits that leave sizing unchanged, no exit is positive in both runs at 15m or 30m.
findings.evidence: exitlab re-run, every house-exit signal of v3b + v4, base = live rule, open positions marked at 10/07 15:40 KST (exitlab_paired.csv / exitlab_base_levels.csv, scripts analyze_exitlab.py and show_levels.py). Net R = gross R minus cost R: 15m n 2,477: -0.106 = +0.062 - 0.168. 30m n 1,277: -0.147 = -0.030 - 0.117. 1h n 780: -0.136 = -0.053 - 0.083. 4h n 112: -0.044 = +0.001 - 0.046. House payoff at 15m: 52.6% wins, average win +0.87R, average loss -1.19R, so breakeven needs 57.8% wins. At 30m: 57.6% wins, +0.56R / -1.10R, breakeven 66.4%. Over 34 exits the pooled 15m mean ranges from -0.225R (tp1.5R) to +0.059R (RL2_1). Best exit in hindsight at 15m: v3b -0.289R (be0.5_tp1), v4 +0.200R (RL2_1). At 30m: v3b -0.159R, v4 +0.030R. The side-flipped (coin-flip) entries lose about as much (15m -0.193R, 30m -0.103R).
findings.implication: Do not expect an exit or custom value to turn a 15m/30m strategy positive. The AI trader has to supply direction or timing edge larger than about 0.17R (15m) or 0.12R (30m) per trade. Exit work should aim at not destroying edge, not at creating it.

findings.claim: The 'lev10 +0.26R / lock30 +0.14R' headline is the ROE ladder's geometry acting during one trending regime, not a robust custom value. The ladder locks net ROE, so its price trigger is 0.12/L + 0.14% and shrinks as leverage L grows. In R units of the 2 ATR stop it arms early and trails very tightly. lev10 and lock30 simply arm later. The effect has the opposite sign across runs.
findings.evidence: Ladder geometry (lev_risk.csv, ladder_geometry.csv), in R at the median stop. 15m (stop 0.62%): trigger at 10x / 20x / 30x / 50x = 2.16 / 1.19 / 0.87 / 0.61R; at 30x the lock is 0.76R and the trail gap after arming is 0.11-0.38R. 1h at 30x: trigger 0.43R, lock 0.38R, trail 0.05-0.19R. The 0.14% cost is 37% of the trigger distance at 50x and 10% at 10x. In R, lev10 = geo10 and lev20m20 = geo20 in every run and tf, so leverage changes R only through the ladder. lev10 vs house at 15m: v3a (nightly shadows, base mostly 50x) +0.460 [0.180, 0.776], n 296. v3b (re-run) -0.230 [-0.397, -0.083], n 407. v4 +0.167 [-0.050, 0.403], n 2,070. Pooled v3b+v4 +0.101 [-0.075, 0.286], q 0.47. lock30 at 15m: +0.210 / -0.233 / +0.008. The pooled headline (+0.26R) is dominated by v3a, which has 1,300 of the 1,462 pairs, 717 of them at 5m (d3_paired_by_run_tf.csv, master_variant_tf.csv).
findings.implication: Do not adopt lev10 or lock30 as custom values on this evidence. The real lesson is structural: an ROE ladder ties the exit to leverage. Under 'leverage by AI confidence' the most confident trades would get the tightest exit (0.61R trigger at 50x vs 1.19R at 20x at 15m).

findings.claim: Picking the best exit per strategy x timeframe in one period and applying it to the next period loses money against simply keeping the house exit. Weekly per-strategy exit tuning on live data would fit noise.
findings.evidence: tuning_oos_summary.csv (tuning_oos.py; the in-sample pick is the highest mean R; the out-of-sample gain is the picked exit minus the house exit). Full menu: v3b to v4, 31 cells: in-sample +0.34R, out-of-sample -0.023 [-0.132, 0.075]. v4 first half to second half, 67 cells: +0.29R in-sample, -0.092 [-0.190, 0.010] out-of-sample. Second half to first half: +0.88R in-sample, -0.210 [-0.288, -0.126] out-of-sample. The tuned exit beat the house exit out-of-sample in only 22-39% of cells. With a 5-exit menu: +0.037, -0.075 and -0.164R out-of-sample. Across the 60 graded cells the exit choice moves a cell's mean by a median of 0.53R (0.16-1.22R). 43 of 60 cells have at least one exit with mean > 0, against only 18 that are positive under the house exit.
findings.implication: Freeze one exit per strategy family for the whole 10/17 to 12/31 test. Run the weekly shadow tuning as a record only. Adopt a new exit only after a pre-registered multi-period (5-year) test, never because it won last week.

findings.claim: The nightly shadow pairing (unresolved rows dropped) is biased against wide exits. The rows it dropped were the wide variants' big winners. Re-running the same v4 trades to the end of the bars removes most of the apparent penalty.
findings.evidence: d3_bias_v4.csv (d3_bias.py): the same 356 / 236 / 126 v4 trades at 15m / 30m / 1h. lev10: shadow pairs -0.213 vs full re-run -0.009 at 15m (bias -0.20R); -0.160 vs +0.071 at 30m; -0.043 vs +0.124 at 1h. tp3R: -0.282 vs -0.089 (15m), -0.463 vs +0.072 (30m), -0.480 vs +0.402 (1h). lock30 at 30m: -0.116 vs +0.026. On the dropped rows the variant minus base averaged +2.13R (lev10, 15m). Validation: exitlab reproduces every resolved nightly variant row exactly (median |dROE| 0, 18 variants, validate_vs_d3.csv) and the rb_analyze replay exactly (4,236 signals, max |dROE| 2.2e-16).
findings.implication: Do not use the d3 shadow tables (or the dashboard boards built on them) to rank exits with long holds. The v3a lev10/lock30 gains are understated, not overstated. Fix the nightly job: extend the horizon, or mark open rows to market and keep them in the pairs.

findings.claim: Which exit wins is a time-clustered regime effect lasting about 12-24 h. The same effect appears on the side-flipped (coin-flip) entries, so it comes from the price path, not from the signals.
findings.evidence: regime_blocks_6h.csv (contrasts.py), 15m+30m signals, wide exit (geo10) minus house in 6 h blocks from 10/05 00:00 UTC: -0.17, -0.10, -0.22, -0.20, -0.48, -0.17, then +0.64, +0.69, +0.39R. Lag-1 correlation +0.61 over 10 blocks (RL2_1 +0.54, RL1_0.5 +0.58). Side-flipped entries show the same wide-exit effect: 15m RL1.5_1 pooled flip +0.174 vs +0.099 for the real side; geo10 flip +0.180 vs +0.101 (master_variant_tf.csv flip_diff_R). A simple trend proxy (efficiency ratio of 15m closes) barely tracks it: correlation 0.15 over 9 blocks (trend_blocks_6h.csv).
findings.implication: A trader rewarded on 1-7 days will see exit styles 'work' and 'fail' by regime. Do not let the AI or the weekly tuner chase the last regime. If a regime switch is ever tried, it needs its own pre-registered test; 10 blocks cannot validate one.

findings.claim: Fixed take-profits at 1-2R are worse than the house ladder at 15m in both runs and not better at 30m. A symmetric 1R target with a 2 ATR stop needs about a 63% hit rate after costs, and the strategies hit about 49%.
findings.evidence: exitlab_paired.csv. tp1.5R vs house at 15m: v3b -0.112, v4 -0.121, pooled -0.120 [-0.212, -0.035]. tp2R: -0.240 / -0.086, pooled -0.111 [-0.207, -0.010]. tp1R: -0.004 / -0.126, pooled -0.106 [-0.228, -0.003]. At 30m: tp1R pooled -0.058 [-0.110, -0.008]; tp1.5R -0.057; tp2R -0.075. Nothing survives BH (q >= 0.135). tp1R at 15m: win 51%, average win +0.70R, average loss -1.17R, payoff 0.595. On the real side, TP 1R came before the stop in 2,090 of 4,242 closed trades (49.3%). 5-year exitstyle: no fixed TP passed its pre-registered rule; at 30m tp1R -0.042% and tp1.5R -0.029% of equity per trade; at 15m small positives of +0.012 to +0.025% (fiveyear_exitstyle_by_tf.csv).
findings.implication: Do not make a fixed 1-2R target the code exit for 15m/30m AI traders. If the AI 'takes profit early like a human', measure that decision on a twin against the code exit; the data says it costs about 0.1R per trade in non-trending periods and gains nothing on average.

findings.claim: Raising the lock only when the strategy's bar closes, effective from the next minute, is slightly better than raising it every minute at 15m/30m. This matches the AI design's rule 3-4.
findings.implication: Keep the design's bar-close lock updates for 15m/30m. The gain is small (+0.02 to +0.04R) and not a reason by itself. At 1h it is slightly negative.

findings.claim: A breakeven move at +1R (stop to the net-zero price including costs) helps exits that otherwise do not protect profit before 1-1.5R, in both runs at 15m. A breakeven before +1R does not help.
findings.implication: If the AI may 'move the stop to breakeven' (allowed action, design 4-2), allow it only after MFE >= +1R and let code compute the net-zero price. Under a ladder that already locks about +0.5R near +1R it is redundant.

findings.claim: Time stops do not help. The house time stop (N bars, lock never armed) was negative at 15m and 1h in 2 of 3 runs, and a 'close if losing at N bars' rule behaves the same. A max hold of 2xN bars is close to neutral.
findings.implication: No time stop in the AI's code exit. A 2xN-bar max hold is acceptable only as an operational safety cap.

findings.claim: Stop width: keep 2 ATR. At fixed size, 2.5-3 ATR stops lose more per unit of base risk in both runs and over 5 years. Under risk-based sizing a wider stop cuts cost per R, but in this data gross R fell by the same amount, so the result is neutral.
findings.implication: Fix the initial stop at 2 ATR14 of the entry timeframe, computed by code. Keep the design's ban on widening. A 1.5 ATR stop is not better and raises cost per R (0.224R vs 0.168R at 15m) under risk sizing.

findings.claim: Leverage 20-50x with margin = leverage% of equity (the rule bot's rule) makes notional = L^2/100 x equity. One 15m stop-out then costs 3.0% (20x), 6.7% (30x), 11.8% (40x) or 18.5% (50x) of equity. Most 40-50x trades fail the 15% cap. The pnl-on-equity 'gains' of low-leverage shadows are smaller bets on negative-EV trades.
findings.evidence: lev_risk.csv. Median loss per stop, 15m / 30m: 20x 3.0 / 4.0%; 30x 6.7 / 9.1%; 40x 11.8 / 16.1%; 50x 18.5 / 25.2%. Share passing the 15% cap and liquidation buffer: 15m 40x 84%, 50x 18%; 30m 40x 37%, 50x 0%; 1h 30x 81%, 40x 1%. Seven straight 15m losses: 19% drawdown at 20x, 38% at 30x, 59% at 40x. pnl on equity per 15m signal: house (mostly 30x) -0.84%, lev10 -0.04%, while geo10 at house size is -0.16% (exitlab_paired.csv). 40x geometry vs house: 15m -0.094R [-0.197, -0.004] (v3b -0.015, v4 -0.105). 5-year: 40x / 50x geometry vs 30x at 15m -0.50 / -1.63 bps per notional, at 1h -2.43 / -4.95 bps; 50x liquidation share 5% (15m) to 19% (1h).
findings.implication: Make the stop and exits independent of leverage. Treat leverage as size: confidence-scaled leverage means confidence-scaled equity risk with no evidence yet that confidence predicts R. Default to fixed risk per stop (the design's 3% twin), or cap 15m/30m at about 30x. Expect 50x to be refused for most 15m and all 30m signals under the 15% cap.

findings.claim: At 1h the house ROE ladder is too tight (arms at about 0.43R, average winner +0.41R, breakeven win rate 71%). Wider geometry beat it in all three live runs and over 5 years. This is the only exit change that is consistent across live runs and the 5-year study.
findings.evidence: geo10 (= lev10) vs house at 1h: v3a +0.298 [0.136, 0.443] (shadows, biased against), v3b +0.145, v4 +0.132; pooled +0.134 [0.001, 0.272], q 0.21. RL2_1 at 1h: +0.263 / +0.218. Resolved-only set: geo10 +0.073 / +0.100. House 1h payoff: 61% wins, +0.41R / -0.99R. 5-year levstop, 10x vs 30x geometry: 1h +1.76 bps per notional (28/36 cells better), 4h +5.76 bps (26/36); 20x vs 30x: 1h +1.08 (29/36), 4h +2.73 (22/36). Live 4h (n 112) disagrees: wide exits were worse, but most 4h trades were still open and marked to market.
findings.implication: For the cost-free 1h/4h rule accounts, and for any later AI on 1h/4h, use a ladder with at least 10-20x price geometry or an R ladder arming at 1.5-2R. Treat it as a pre-registered change with its own shadow, not an in-run switch.

findings.claim: Per strategy x tf, no cell has every-signal house R significantly above 0 after BH. Two cells are significantly negative. Only three cells keep a positive mean under every exit tested (exit-robust sign), and 17 cells are negative under every exit.
findings.evidence: strategy_tf_exits.csv (60 cells with >= 25 every-signal entries; 1 h-cluster bootstrap; BH). Best q 0.72. BH-negative: F4_PULL 15m -0.59 [-0.89, -0.24] (q 0.05, n 52); N18_VWMA_MACD 30m -0.74 [-0.99, -0.42] (q 0.004, n 43). Positive under all 34 exits: N17_KC_RSI 15m +0.16 [-0.11, 0.42] (n 153; v3b +0.61 at n 15, v4 +0.11 at n 138; spread across exits only 0.16R); N20_EMA9_CHOP 30m +0.26 [-0.11, 0.67] (n 43); F6_VWAP_CROSS 1h +0.11 [-0.13, 0.30] (n 43, v4 only). Grades: 18 C, 40 D, 2 F, no A or B.
findings.implication: Use exit robustness as a screening criterion for AI candidates: prefer cells whose sign does not depend on the exit (N17_KC_RSI 15m, N20_EMA9_CHOP 30m). Treat cells that are positive only under a hindsight exit as unproven. Drop F4_PULL 15m and N18_VWMA_MACD 30m from AI consideration.

findings.claim: The every-signal exit re-run is trustworthy as a measuring tool. It matches the live engine and the nightly shadows exactly. 7-12% of positions are still open at the data end, and their mark-to-market does not drive the conclusions.
findings.evidence: validate.txt. Base vs rb_analyze replay: 4,236 closed signals, max |dROE| 2.2e-16, same exit reasons. 410 rb_analyze-unresolved signals now resolve (89) or are marked (321). 102 sizing rejections match. Every resolved nightly variant row on v4 trades matches exactly (median |dROE| 0, 18 variants). Open at the end on the real side: base 321 of 4,646 (6.9%), RL2_1 519 (11.2%), tp3R 561 (12.1%). On the all-resolved subset the per-run differences are close (e.g. RL1.5_1 15m v4 +0.164 all vs +0.183 resolved; exitlab_robustness.csv dR_res_*).
findings.implication: Use exitlab.py (copied engine calls, no repo edits) as the template for the nightly shadow fix and for the pre-registered 5-year test of the AI exit (R ladder, BE at 1R, bar-close updates) before 10/17.

limits: Live evidence covers only about 4.8 days in three regimes: v3a 10/02-10/05, v3b 0.7 days, v4 1.5 days. The exit effects at 15m/30m flip sign between consecutive 6-24 h windows, so the live data cannot estimate any exit's long-run effect. It can only show that effects are regime-dependent and that no exit fixes cost plus the lack of edge.

v3a has no live_bars, so it cannot be re-run. Its numbers come from nightly shadows on entered trades only, with unresolved rows dropped (biased against wide exits, shown on v4: -0.20R for lev10 at 15m). The v3a base was the 50x tier walk, so v3a variant differences are relative to a different (tighter) geometry than v3b/v4 at 30x.

The re-run horizon ends at 10/07 15:40 KST. Positions still open then are marked to market with exit costs: 6.9% of house trades, 11-12% for the widest exits (RL2_1, tp3R). This is unbiased only if prices are a martingale. 4h results are dominated by such marks, and 1h results partly; the all-resolved subset agrees in sign but selects on resolution time.

Time-cluster bootstrap with 1 h blocks gives only 17 clusters for v3b and 36-37 for v4, so CIs are approximate and probably too narrow. Signals duplicated across DeepSeek definitions and accounts are kept per account and add no independent information. No variant or contrast survives BH at 0.05 (the best q is about 0.09).

The new exit candidates (R-unit ladders, BE at 1R, bar-close updates, time_neg, max hold) were tested only on these days. The repo's 5-year studies cover only the ROE-ladder geometry (levstop fixed-leverage arms) and fixed TPs (exitstyle). Before 10/17 the R ladder needs a pre-registered 5-year test; this analysis does not provide one (5-year bars are not in this container; Binance is blocked from here).

Funding rates were solved from recorded trade funding and brackets were inferred from trades (as in rb_analyze). A replayed position held over a funding instant no live trade held pays 0 funding. Paper stop slippage (2 bps) is used; measured real stop slips were slightly smaller, so stop-heavy exits are, if anything, penalized a little.

Every variant runs each signal alone on a fresh $5,000 account. One-position accounts would take fewer signals, and shorter exits free the slot for more trades and more costs. Account-level effects of exit length (trades per day, cost drag) are not simulated.

AI discretionary behavior (early profit-taking, switching, near-signal entries, confidence-scaled leverage) cannot be simulated from rule data. The tight-vs-wide exit results only bound what mechanical analogues of those behaviors did in these regimes.

Strategy x tf cells have 25-153 signals (v3b at most 43 per cell; DeepSeek v4-only). Grades are descriptive; no cell is decidable on its own, and 'best exit in hindsight' per cell is mostly noise (out-of-sample test X3).

## Exits, stop width, leverage and the profit-lock ladder: which custom values help

### Summary

The house exit is not why 15m and 30m lose money. On every signal, the result before costs is about zero, and the round-trip cost (0.17R at 15m, 0.12R at 30m) is the loss. Here 1R = the planned loss at the 2 ATR stop.

The reported gains for 10x leverage (+0.26R) and a later first lock at 30% ROE (+0.14R) are not robust custom values. Both work by arming the profit lock later. That paid in one trending window and lost in the next run: at 15m, +0.46R in v3a, -0.23R in v3b, +0.17R in v4. The nightly shadow tables also understate the wide exits, because they drop trades that were still open.

Choosing a different exit per strategy from recent data lost 0.02-0.21R per trade out-of-sample.

What survives across runs:
- Fixed 1-2R take-profits are worse than the house ladder at 15m.
- Time stops do not help.
- A 2.5-3 ATR stop is worse than 2 ATR at the same size.
- Breakeven helps only from +1R.
- Raising the lock only at bar close is slightly better at 15m/30m.
- At 1h the house ladder is clearly too tight. This is the only change consistent across 3 live runs and the 5-year study.

Leverage changes R only through the profit-lock ladder. As size, 40-50x is either refused by the 15% loss cap or risks 12-25% of equity per stop.

Recommendation: exits and stops must be computed in price/R terms and must not depend on leverage. Freeze one exit per strategy family for the whole test. Run the candidate exits as shadows.

### Data and method

- **What was simulated.** Every submitted signal of the house-exit accounts (36 core strategies, DeepSeek, coin flips) at 15m/30m/1h/4h in v3b and v4: 4,748 signals, each run alone through the repo's own `PaperEngine` on the 1m `live_bars`. 39 exits, plus the same signal with the side flipped (a coin flip at the same moment): 362,592 runs.
- **Horizon.** v3b's bars were extended with v4's bars, so v3b signals have at least 36 h. Positions open at 10/07 15:40 KST are marked to market with exit costs (status OPEN_END). Every exit is therefore evaluated on the same set of signals.
- **Validation.**
  - The base matches the rb_analyze replay exactly: 4,236 signals, max |dROE| 2.2e-16.
  - Every resolved nightly shadow row on v4 trades is reproduced exactly: 18 variants, median |dROE| 0.
  - Files: `validate.txt`, `validate_vs_d3.csv`.
- **Units.** R is in units of the base 2 ATR stop: pnl / (qty × |entry − base stop|). "pe" = pnl as % of a fresh $5,000 account; an entry refused by sizing counts as 0.
- **Statistics.** CIs are cluster bootstraps over 1 h blocks of signal time (all coins together), with 4 h blocks as a check. BH correction across the pooled variant × timeframe tests.
- **v3a.** It has no live_bars, so it is shown only from the nightly shadows. Those cover entered trades only, drop unresolved rows, and the base was mostly 50x.
- **Exit names used below.**
  - `geoL`: the house ladder computed as if leverage were L, at the real size.
  - `RLa_b`: R ladder; lock +b R once the best excursion (MFE) reaches +a R, then raise in steps.
  - `_bar`: the lock is raised only when the strategy's bar closes.
  - `be1_*`: breakeven at +1R.
  - `timestop`: market exit after N bars if the lock never armed.
  - `time_neg`: exit at N bars if losing.
  - `max2x`: hard exit after 2N bars.
  - `stopwk`: stop at k ATR.
  - `tpkR`: fixed take-profit at k R, no ladder.

### 1. Is the house exit the loss source? No.

Every signal, v3b + v4 pooled (`exitlab_paired.csv`, `exitlab_base_levels.csv`):

| tf | n | net R | gross R | cost R | win % | avg win R | avg loss R | payoff | breakeven win % | mean R over the 34 exits (range) | best exit in hindsight v3b / v4 | flipped side net R |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15m | 2,477 | -0.106 | +0.062 | 0.168 | 52.6 | +0.87 | -1.19 | 0.73 | 57.8 | -0.225 (tp1.5R) to +0.059 (RL2_1) | be0.5_tp1 -0.289 / RL2_1 +0.200 | -0.193 |
| 30m | 1,277 | -0.147 | -0.030 | 0.117 | 57.6 | +0.56 | -1.10 | 0.51 | 66.4 | -0.222 (tp2R) to -0.043 (RL1.5_1_bar) | geo50 -0.159 / RL1.5_1_bar +0.030 | -0.103 |
| 1h | 780 | -0.136 | -0.053 | 0.083 | 61.0 | +0.41 | -0.99 | 0.41 | 70.7 | -0.171 (timestop) to +0.180 (be1_tp3) | tp3R +0.070 / be1_tp3 +0.269 | -0.121 |
| 4h | 112 | -0.044 | +0.001 | 0.046 | 56.2 | +0.50 | -0.74 | 0.67 | 59.8 | (mostly open, marked) | n/a | +0.037 |

- **A stop-out costs about 1.19R at 15m, not 1R.** The extra is costs plus stop slippage.
- **The ladder's winners are small, and smallest on higher timeframes:** +0.87R at 15m, +0.41R at 1h. Breakeven therefore needs 58-71% winners.
- **Even the best exit in hindsight loses in v3b at 15m/30m.** The best exit flips between "tight" (v3b) and "wide" (v4).
- **No exit has a positive expectation without edge.** Under no edge every exit has expected gross R ≈ 0, and the coin-flip side loses about as much.

### 2. Why the ROE ladder rewarded 10x and a 30% first lock

The ladder locks net ROE. Its first trigger is at a price move of 0.12/L + 0.14%, so it shrinks with leverage L and ignores volatility (ATR). In R of the live 2 ATR stop (`lev_risk.csv`, medians over v3b+v4 signals):

| tf | median stop | trigger R at 10x / 20x / 30x / 50x | first lock at 30x | trail gap after arming at 30x |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15m | 0.62% | 2.16 / 1.19 / 0.87 / 0.61 | 0.76R | 0.11-0.38R |
| 30m | 0.89% | 1.51 / 0.84 / 0.61 / 0.43 | 0.53R | 0.08-0.26R |
| 1h | 1.25% | 1.07 / 0.59 / 0.43 / 0.30 | 0.38R | 0.05-0.19R |
| 4h (20x) | 2.02% | 0.67 / 0.37 / 0.27 / 0.19 | 0.32R at 20x | 0.05-0.17R at 20x |

- **Costs eat the high-leverage trigger.** The 0.14% round trip is 37% of the 50x trigger distance and 10% of the 10x one.
- **At high leverage the ladder is a very tight trail.** Once armed it follows the price within 0.1-0.4R on 15m and within 0.05-0.2R on 1h.
- **lev10 and lock30 are the same lever: arm later.** In R, `lev10` equals `geo10` and `lev20m20` equals `geo20` in every run and timeframe; at 10-30x leverage acts only through this geometry. `lock30` at 30x arms at about 2R on 15m.
