   - Over 5 years, 1.5-2 ATR is best per notional.
   - Live, 2.5-3 ATR was worse in both runs at the same size (15m stopw3 -0.051 [-0.097, -0.001]).
   - 1.5 ATR is no better (+0.004R at 15m) and raises cost per R under risk sizing (0.224 vs 0.168R).
2. **Profit protection that does not depend on leverage, raised only at the strategy-bar close and effective from the next minute.** Evidence for the ladder choice: low (neither option differs reliably from the house exit). Evidence for bar-close updates: low-medium (+0.02 to +0.04R at 15m/30m, CI excludes 0 pooled, q ≈ 0.09).
   - **Default (the AI design's choice):** the house ladder at fixed 20x price geometry. Arm at +0.74% (12%/20 + 0.14%), lock +0.64%, then steps of 0.25% of price. At the median stop that is about 1.2R / 1.03R at 15m and 0.84R / 0.72R at 30m.
     - Live vs the house exit: +0.056 (15m) and +0.059 (30m, the same sign in both runs).
     - 5-year: equivalent to 30x.
   - **Shadow candidate:** R ladder `RL1_0.5_bar` (arm at MFE ≥ +1R, lock +0.5R, +0.5R per +0.5R). It is volatility-normalized and equal across coins.
     - Live: +0.125 [0.014, 0.267] at 15m, but v3b -0.074 and v4 +0.165.
     - Adopt it only if a pre-registered 5-year test passes.
3. **No fixed 1-2R take-profit as the code exit.** Evidence: medium against.
   - 15m tp1.5R -0.120 [-0.212, -0.035] and tp2R -0.111 [-0.207, -0.010], negative in both runs.
   - A 1R target needs a 63% hit rate; the strategies hit 49.3%.
4. **Breakeven only after MFE ≥ +1R, to the net-zero price including costs.** Evidence: low-medium. It adds +0.05 to +0.08R to target exits in both runs at 15m. Breakeven at +0.5R hurt in v4 (-0.143).
5. **No time stop.** Evidence: medium against. 15m -0.045 [-0.100, -0.004]; 1h -0.036 [-0.069, -0.007]; negative in 2 of 3 runs. A 2N-bar max hold is neutral (-0.017R) and acceptable only as a safety cap.
6. **Leverage must not touch the exit.**
   - With margin = leverage %, keep a 15m/30m stop-out at about 7% of equity or less (30x at 15m, 20-30x at 30m).
   - Scale confidence through risk per stop, not through the ladder, and keep the fixed-risk twin.
   - 40-50x adds risk without any evidence that confidence predicts R. 40x geometry was -0.094R at 15m, and 50x is refused for 82% (15m) and 100% (30m) of signals.
   - Evidence: high on the arithmetic, medium on R.
7. **Freeze exits for the whole test; tune only in shadow; adopt only through a multi-period pre-registered test.** Evidence: high (out-of-sample loss of per-cell tuning, section 4).
8. **For the 1h/4h rule accounts:** widen the ladder to at least 10-20x geometry, or use an R ladder arming at 1.5-2R. Run it as a pre-registered shadow first. Evidence: medium (1h geo10 positive in v3a, v3b and v4, and 28/36 cells over 5 years).

### 8. Strategy × timeframe through the exit lens

`strategy_tf_exits.csv` covers 60 cells with at least 25 every-signal entries.

- **No cell is significantly positive after BH** (best q 0.72).
- **Two cells are significantly negative:** F4_PULL 15m -0.59 (q 0.05) and N18_VWMA_MACD 30m -0.74 (q 0.004).
- **Exit choice moves a cell a lot:** a median of 0.53R, up to 1.22R. 43 cells are positive under some exit but only 18 under the house exit, so cells that are "positive under the right exit" are unproven.
- **Positive under all 34 exits (exit-robust sign):**
  - N17_KC_RSI 15m: n 153, +0.16 [-0.11, 0.42], both runs positive, spread 0.16R.
  - N20_EMA9_CHOP 30m: n 43, +0.26 [-0.11, 0.67].
  - F6_VWAP_CROSS 1h: n 43, v4 only.
- **Negative under every exit:** 17 cells, e.g. N22_VORTEX_PSAR, OBV_B, N25_DST_CCI and N18_VWMA_MACD at 15m; N04_ST_KLINGER and S2_ST_ROC at all timeframes.

### What the data cannot tell

- The long-run value of any 15m/30m exit. Live effects flip with 12-24 h regimes, and the new candidates have no 5-year test.
- Anything about v3a beyond the biased nightly shadows (no live_bars).
- 4h, and partly 1h, results beyond the 10/07 data end (marked positions).
- Account-level effects: how exit length changes trades per day and cost drag in one-position accounts.
- How discretionary AI exits will behave.

Treat these numbers as evidence about structure (cost, leverage coupling, overfitting risk), not as tuned values.

findings.claim: At 15m and 30m the paper losses are the round-trip cost and nothing else: before fees and slippage the signals earn about zero. Fees, the 2 bp paper slippage per side and funding take 0.18 to 0.26 R per trade. No live trade was liquidated.
findings.evidence: Live trades, all runs (c01_decompose.py -> out/c01_decomp_by_tf.csv), core36 15m n=630: net -0.190R = gross +0.072R - cost 0.262R (fees 0.187, entry slip 0.0375, exit slip 0.0375, funding 0.0000). 30m n=378: -0.152 = +0.024 - 0.176. 1h n=212: -0.073 = +0.042 - 0.115. ds200 15m n=259: -0.288 = -0.043 - 0.245; ds200 30m n=181: -0.126 = +0.045 - 0.171. The R identity is checked per trade (max error 1e-12). 0 LIQ exits in 2,651 strategy-kind trades. Every SUBMITTED signal replayed alone (v3b+v4, c02_replay.py, parity 4,236/4,236 to 1e-9 vs replay_signals.csv; c05_breakeven.py -> c05_breakeven_by_tf.csv), core36+ds200 15m n=2,424 in 54 clusters: net -0.103R, gross +0.132R [cluster CI +0.001, +0.286], paper cost 0.236R. 30m n=1,259: net -0.144, gross +0.020 [-0.072, +0.113], cost 0.163.
findings.implication: An AI trader that takes these signals gets no pre-cost edge to build on. Every R of profit has to come from the AI's own entry, direction, skip and exit decisions, and those decisions must first pay about 0.16 to 0.24 R per round trip.

findings.claim: Over five years each of the 36 strategies' signals lost almost exactly one paper round trip (about -14 bp of notional) at every timeframe, in every year, on every coin, in both periods and in every volatility quintile. The gross edge is zero, and the side choice adds nothing over a coin flip.
findings.evidence: c07_5y_regime.py (repo's research/levstop.outcomes -> strategy_profiles._scan, fixed 30x, 2 ATR stop, paper ladder; signal cache verified identical to paperbot/agents/labdata_reference.json, 18/18 files; out/c07_5y_regime.csv). 15m n=1,140,655 signals, 271 weeks: net -14.24 bp/notional [week-block CI -14.75, -13.71], gross +0.04 bp, gross R +0.0013 [-0.0052, +0.0082], side-choice excess vs opposite side +0.0031R [-0.0020, +0.0084]. 30m n=573,097: net -15.33 bp, gross -0.91 bp, gross R -0.0017 [-0.0079, +0.0050]. 1h n=287,925: net -17.45 bp, gross -2.8 bp. Net per year at 15m from 2021 to 2026: -13.7, -14.1, -15.1, -13.8, -14.8, -13.5 bp. Per coin: -13.6 (DOGE) to -14.9 (BTC). Volatility quintiles Q1 to Q5: -14.0, -13.7, -14.6, -14.1, -14.7 bp. levstop.json shows the same at fixed 10x, 20x and 30x: -14.4, -14.4 and -14.5 bp/notional.
findings.implication: No coin, year or volatility filter turns these signals into a pre-cost edge. The AI's added value must be measured in gross bp per round trip against a timing-matched coin flip, and it has to beat about 10 to 19 bp before anything is earned.

findings.claim: To break even, the AI must add this much gross edge per trade at today's volatility: 15m 0.16 to 0.29 R with real taker execution (0.10 to 0.17 R with maker entries, if fills were not adversely selected); 30m 0.11 to 0.22 R (0.07 to 0.13 R with maker entries). In price terms that is 10 to 19 bp per round trip as a taker and about 7 to 12 bp with a maker entry.
findings.evidence: c10_needed_edge.py -> out/c10_needed_edge.csv (needed R = measured round-trip bps / live median stop bps - max(5y gross R, 0)). 15m real taker: SOL 0.155, DOGE 0.160, LTC 0.212, BTC 0.215, ETH 0.218, BCH 0.292; maker entry + taker stop: DOGE 0.096, SOL 0.098, LTC 0.118, BTC 0.151, ETH 0.152, BCH 0.172. 30m real taker: DOGE 0.114, SOL 0.116, LTC 0.149, ETH 0.150, BTC 0.151, BCH 0.216; maker: DOGE 0.070, SOL 0.074, LTC 0.083, ETH 0.105, BTC 0.106, BCH 0.130. findings.implication: The best five-year pre-cost edge of any core strategy is about +0.02R, and the live side choice adds -0.005R. The AI would have to be about ten times better than anything measured so far. That is a strong prior against profitable 15m AI traders before 12/31. 30m is the more feasible of the two.

findings.claim: Today's market is unusually quiet: the live 2 ATR stop sits at the 16th to 18th percentile of five years. That makes costs in R about 1.7 times their five-year typical size.

Live median stop: 15m 0.620% (5y median 1.035%, 17.8th percentile), 30m 0.886% (1.496%, 16.1st), 1h 1.244% (2.174%, 13.5th), 4h 2.016% (4.593%, 3.8th). Under risk-based sizing, skipping the quietest regime cuts losses per R. It does not create profit.

findings.claim: An average stop-loss costs -1.23R at 15m instead of -1R. The overshoot is almost entirely fees plus the paper's 2 bp exit slippage; real gaps through the initial stop are negligible.
findings.evidence: c01_decompose.py -> out/c01_sl_decomposition_by_tf.csv (core36+ds200 SL exits). 15m n=417: R -1.235 = -1 - fees 0.194 - exit slip 0.039 - gap 0.0002 - funding 0.0013. The 2 bp entry slip (0.039R) is inside the 1R unit because R is measured from the fill. 30m n=220: -1.157 (fees 0.130, slip 0.026). 1h n=101: -1.108. 4h n=14: -1.058. 5m n=497: -1.573. Exactly at stop - 2 bp: 99.5% (15m), 99.6% (30m), 100% (1h).
findings.implication: The overshoot is 12 to 14 bp divided by the stop %, so it is a stop-width problem, not an execution bug. At 20-50x the extra -0.2R per loss is real money. The AI's exit code should budget each stop at -(1 + cost/stop) R.

findings.claim: Real execution at the paper size (about $45k notional) costs 10.1 to 10.2 bp per round trip on BTC/ETH, 11.0 on SOL, 12.4 on DOGE, 16.0 on LTC and 19.3 on BCH, against 14 bp in paper. Paper is right on average, but it flatters LTC and BCH because their books are thin.

Real stop-market slip on SL exits (d3_stop_slips, v4, status ok): BTC 0.09 bp (n=57), ETH 0.17 (28), SOL 0.93 (44), DOGE 1.74 (17), LTC 3.34 (26), BCH 4.91 (42). Every-signal replay with per-coin real costs on the same price path changes the core36 result by +0.000R at 15m [-0.044, +0.045] and +0.020R at 30m (c04_scenarios.csv).
findings.implication: Do not trade BCH or LTC at $20-125k notional (20-50x on $5k with margin = leverage %), or cut the order size. At the small real-money size, the book walk mostly disappears and real taker cost falls to about 10-12 bp on every coin.

findings.claim: Per unit of risk, SOL and DOGE are the cheapest coins to trade at 15m/30m. BTC and ETH have the lowest costs in bp but the tightest stops, so their cost per R is high. BCH is the worst coin at the current order size.

findings.claim: Maker (limit) entries recover little because the fills are adversely selected: the limit order tends to fill on losing trades and miss winning ones. On fixed exits, the fee and slippage saving would be worth about +0.06R per trade, but after missed winners the net gain is about 0 to +0.1R.

Nightly d3 limit shadow joined to the market replay (c08_limit_d3.py -> c08_limit_d3.csv, v4): fill 62-74%; the missed signals were 63-80% winners at market (+0.07 to +0.30R); fills improved by +0.16 to +0.23R; net per signal vs market: core 15m +0.097 [-0.009, +0.198], core 30m +0.097 [+0.010, +0.199], ds200 +0.015/+0.007, pooled +0.045 [-0.037, +0.125]; net per signal still -0.08 to -0.14R. 5-year maker study (research/maker/RESULTS_ROUND2.md): +3 to +8 bp per trade, still negative, fill 76-77% at 0.25 ATR.

findings.claim: Wider stops (2.5 or 3 ATR) do not reduce the cost that matters. With leverage-based sizing, the notional and therefore the dollar cost stay the same, and the bigger losses make the dollar result worse. With risk-based sizing, the result per R is unchanged.
findings.evidence: c04_scenarios.csv (same leverage, every signal). Core36 15m in base-R units: w25 -0.029 [-0.063, +0.012], w30 -0.058 [-0.114, +0.006]; in own-R units -0.126/-0.125 vs base -0.128. 30m: -0.020/-0.044 (own R -0.134/-0.127 vs -0.146). ds200 15m w30 -0.062 [-0.118, -0.003]. The nightly d3 stopw variants are mixed (pipeline summary: core 15m stopw2.5 -0.054, stopw3 -0.038; ds200 30m +0.063/+0.099). 5-year levstop: at 30x, going from 2 to 3 ATR moves the pooled P&L per trade from -1.30% to -1.36% of equity; at 10x the per-notional result goes from -14.4 to -14.8 bp.
findings.implication: Custom-value tuning of the stop width is not a cost fix. Cost per R falls only if the notional falls with it (risk-based sizing), and then the gross R falls by the same amount.

findings.claim: Leverage turns the fixed 14 bp into an equity drag that grows with leverage times margin share. At 50x with margin = 50%, every round trip costs 3.5% of the account, so three trades a day cost 10.5% of equity per day before any edge.
findings.evidence: c05_breakeven.py -> out/c05_ai_leverage_cost.csv. Paper cost per trade as % of equity with margin = leverage %: 10x 0.14, 20x 0.56, 30x 1.26, 40x 2.24, 50x 3.50 (real BTC: 0.40/0.91/1.62/2.53 at 20/30/40/50x). With a fixed 20% margin, 50x costs 1.40%. 5-year levstop (fixed leverage, 2 ATR): per-notional -14.4 (10x), -14.4 (20x), -14.5 (30x), -14.9 (40x), -15.7 bp (50x); liquidated share 0.01%, 0.21%, 0.79%, 2.05%, 4.14%.
findings.implication: 'Leverage 20-50x by AI confidence' only pays if the AI's confidence predicts at least 14 bp of gross edge. Otherwise moving from 20x/20% to 50x/50% multiplies the cost drag by 6.25. Size leverage on a measured gross edge and keep the 50x tier off until that is shown.

findings.claim: The code-computed lock ladder leaks about 0.09 to 0.11R on every lock exit. In 37% of lock exits the next 1m bar opens beyond the new lock level, because at 30x the ladder's 2% ROE trigger gap is only about 6.7 bp of price, about one minute of noise.
findings.evidence: c01_decompose.py -> out/c01_lock_gap_by_tf.csv (core36+ds200 LOCK exits, live trades). 15m n=472: 37.5% gapped, mean 6.5 bp (p90 12.8), 0.115R per lock exit. 30m n=339: 37.2%, 8.0 bp (p90 19.1), 0.090R. 1h n=214: 36.5%, 8.9 bp, 0.076R. Median 1m bar range 3.3-7.1 bp (c00_ticks.csv). Real stop data on LOCK exits matches paper on average (d3 LOCK real minus paper -0.3 bp at 15m/30m, pipeline stop_slips_summary.csv), so the leak is real, not a paper artifact.
findings.implication: For AI exits computed by code, place the exchange-side stop the moment a lock arms (tick or mark stream) instead of at the next 1m bar, or make the lock steps price-based and wider than one minute of noise. That could recover up to about 0.05R per trade (an upper bound; the counterfactual path cannot be replayed on 1m bars).

findings.claim: The positive live gross at 15m (+0.13R) does not come from strategy skill. Coin flips earned it too: the tight-lock, wide-stop exits gain in a quiet, ranging market. Five years show no such gain, even in the quietest quintile.

The pipeline's side-flip shows both sides at the same moments net about -0.15R at 15m (strategy chosen -0.152 vs other side -0.165). 5-year average of both sides ('coinflip_gross_R', c07_5y_regime.csv): 15m -0.0018R overall, Q1 quietest -0.0022.
findings.implication: Do not read October's 15m paper gross as an edge an AI can keep. When volatility returns, the same exit structure is expected to give that gross back.

findings.claim: 'Trading like a human' makes cost worse. Every extra round trip (a switch, a re-entry, a split entry) costs another 0.16 to 0.30R at 15m. On lock winners, costs already eat about a quarter of the gross, so taking profit earlier raises that share.
findings.evidence: Paper cost per round trip in R (c05_breakeven_by_tf.csv): 15m 0.236, 30m 0.163, 1h 0.116, 4h 0.064. Lock-exit winners (c01_lock_gap_by_tf.csv): 15m gross 0.92R, cost 0.24R (26%); 30m gross 0.68R, cost 0.17R (25%). Funding is negligible at 15m/30m (0.000-0.001R per trade, c01).
findings.implication: Make 'skip' the AI's default action and add trade-count limits per trader. Score switching and early exits against the extra cost they cause, and count every AI action that adds a round trip at about 0.2R at 15m.

limits: The live data covers about 4.8 days (v3a 2.6, v3b 0.7, v4 1.5) of one quiet, mostly falling market. Per strategy x tf, live n is usually under 50 and the cluster CIs span about +-0.3 to 1R, so live cells can only be cross-checked. The grades rest on five-year gross edges.
The every-signal replays and the cost scenarios cover only v3b and v4 (v3a has no live_bars). Live-trade decompositions cover all three runs.

Real entry cost (fill_costs.slip_best) is the order-book walk at the paper size of about $45k notional, read a few seconds after the minute. Latency drift between the signal-ready reference price and a real order is NOT measured. At a small real-money size the book walk is about 0 for every coin, so LTC/BCH would look better than shown here.

The real stop slip (d3_stop_slips) exists only for v4 nights. 451 of 761 stop exits have an estimate; 'cap' rows (the fetch limit) are excluded, which tilts the sample toward the largest exits. SL-only samples per coin are small (DOGE 17, LTC 26, ETH 28).

The spread is taken as one price tick inferred from live_bars, and maker fills use a trade-through rule. Queue position, partial fills, post-only rejections and Binance's 'order would immediately trigger' error for lock stops are not modelled.

Maker-entry what-ifs differ in timing. My replay rests the order from the first full minute after the signal (conservative); the nightly d3 limit shadow starts in the signal-ready minute (optimistic) and shifts the stop. Both use 1m bars, so in-minute ordering is unknown.

The fixed-ladder cost scenarios keep the 14 bp lock formula, but a changed entry fill still moves lock prices by about 2 bp. Per-coin scenario differences are therefore noisy, and the break-even figures use the accounting method (same exits, costs swapped).

The five-year runs use the repo's research engine on 15m/30m/1h bars (not 1m), a fixed 30x (liquidation-clipped stops at high volatility, which hurts 1h Q5), taker 5 bp + 2 bp slip and funding 0.01%/8h. They describe every signal alone, not one-position accounts. DeepSeek five-year gross uses its own PREREG exits (unlevered %), not the house ladder.

The grades are not multiple-testing corrected. With 108 core cells, about 3 'B' cells are expected by chance, and the three B cells found are at that level. Strategies with no live signals in v3b/v4 at a timeframe were not graded.

The lock-gap leak (0.09-0.11R per lock exit) is measured against the lock level. What a tick-level exchange stop would actually have achieved cannot be replayed on 1m bars, so the about 0.05R/trade recovery is an upper bound.

Power: per-trade SD at 15m is 1.31R with a design effect of about 7.4 (54 clusters); at 30m it is 0.91R with about 3.6. Detecting an AI gross improvement of +0.15R at 80% power needs about 4,400 trades at 15m or about 1,000 at 30m. A single AI trader cannot verify the required edge by 12/31; only pooled AI traders with side-flip controls can.
Funding was inferred from the trades (pipeline) and is about 0 at 15m/30m. A funding spike regime was not observed and could matter for holds of 4h and longer.

## Costs, slippage and execution: can 15m/30m survive costs?

**Short answer.** No: not with these signals, and not without a large new edge. At 15m and 30m the rule bot's losses are almost exactly its round-trip costs. Before costs the signals earn about zero, both in October's live paper data and in five years of history.

To break even, an AI trader would have to add a gross edge of about **10-19 bp of price per round trip**. At today's (unusually quiet) volatility that is **+0.16 to +0.29 R per trade at 15m** and **+0.11 to +0.22 R at 30m**. Maker entries lower this to about +0.10-0.17 R and +0.07-0.13 R, but only if fills are not adversely selected, and they are.

For scale: the best pre-cost edge any core strategy showed over five years is about +0.02 R, and the strategies' choice of long or short adds about 0 over a coin flip.

All numbers below come from scripts in `scratchpad/lens/costs/` (outputs in `out/`). R = net pnl / (qty x |fill - initial stop|), as in the pipeline.

### 1. Where the 15m/30m losses go (live trades, all runs)

The small positive gross at 15m is not skill. The coin flips earned more, and both sides of the same signals net about -0.15 R in the pipeline's side-flip test. It is what tight ladder locks plus a wide stop earn in a quiet, ranging market.

### 2. Why a stop-loss costs -1.23 R instead of -1 R

`out/c01_sl_decomposition_by_tf.csv` (core36 + ds200 SL exits). 99.5-100% of SL exits fill exactly at stop - 2 bp; 1m bars almost never gap through the initial stop.

| tf | n | mean SL R | fees | exit slip | gap | funding | median stop % |

| 5m | 497 | -1.573 | 0.476 | 0.095 | 0.001 | 0.001 | 0.27 |
| 15m | 417 | -1.235 | 0.194 | 0.039 | 0.000 | 0.001 | 0.58 |

| 4h | 14 | -1.058 | 0.046 | 0.009 | 0.000 | 0.002 | 2.26 |

The overshoot is (12 bp fees + 2 bp exit slip) / stop %. The 2 bp entry slip sits inside the 1 R unit, because R is measured from the fill and the stop is placed from the reference price.

**Lock exits leak too** (`out/c01_lock_gap_by_tf.csv`). In 37% of LOCK exits the next 1m bar opens beyond the newly raised lock, because the ladder raises the stop after the bar, from its high. That costs 6.5 bp (15m), 8.0 bp (30m) and 8.9 bp (1h) per lock exit, or 0.115 / 0.090 / 0.076 R. At 30x the ladder's 2% ROE trigger gap is only about 6.7 bp of price, about one minute of noise (median 1m range 3.3-7.1 bp). On lock winners, costs eat about a quarter of the gross: 15m 0.24 of 0.92 R, 30m 0.17 of 0.68 R.

### 3. Five years: the loss is the round trip, in every regime

**Maker / limit entries: adverse selection eats most of the saving.**

My replay (`c04_scenarios.csv`) and the nightly d3 limit shadow (`c08_limit_d3.csv`):

**BNB fee discount** (4.5 bp taker): +0.016 R (15m), +0.031 R (30m).

**Coin restriction** to SOL/DOGE (plus BTC/ETH at a small notional): saves about 0.04-0.12 R vs including BCH.

**Fixing the lock gap**: up to about 0.05 R/trade (upper bound).

Stacked, these levers might cut the 15m bill from about 0.23 R to about 0.12-0.15 R. They cannot make a zero-gross signal positive.

The B cells earn +1.8 to +2.9 bp before costs (13-21% of one round trip). With 108 core cells, about 3 such cells are expected by chance.

Several live "winners" lose before costs over five years: N17_KC_RSI 15m (live gross +0.35 R [+0.06, +0.62], five-year -0.020 R [-0.031, -0.008]); N20_EMA9_CHOP 30m (+0.42 vs -0.011, both periods negative); OBV_S 30m (+0.74, n=8, vs -0.012); S4_BB_BBP 15m (+0.67 vs -0.013).

### 10. What this means for the AI traders

1. **Timeframe.** Prefer 30m to 15m: the cost per R is about 30% lower and the needed edge is 0.11-0.15 R instead of 0.16-0.22 R on the good coins. Keep 1h/4h as cost-free rule accounts; they are cheap per R but have no five-year gross either.
2. **Coins.** SOL and DOGE are cheapest per R. Use BTC/ETH at a small notional. Avoid BCH and LTC at a large notional.
3. **Strategy base.** Only N07_ICHI_CMO 30m, N12_ICHI_AO 30m and N02_ST_KST 15m bring any pre-cost edge, and it is tiny. D-graded strategies and DeepSeek definitions are poor bases whatever their October results.
4. **Leverage.** Do not scale to 40-50x on 'confidence' until the AI's gross edge is measured at 14 bp or more per round trip against a timing-matched coin flip. Every 50x/50% trade costs 3.5% of equity up front.
5. **Human-like behaviour.** Every switch or re-entry costs another 0.16-0.30 R at 15m. Make 'skip' the default and cap the trade count.
6. **Exit code.** Place the exchange stop the moment a lock arms (the 1m lock gap leaks 0.09-0.11 R per lock exit). Budget each stop at -(1 + cost/stop) R.
7. **Verification.** Detecting a +0.15 R gross improvement needs about 1,000 trades at 30m (SD 0.91 R, design effect 3.6) and about 4,400 at 15m. Pool the AI traders, log the opposite-side shadow for every AI entry, and judge them in gross bp per round trip.

findings.claim: None of the 9 pre-declared discretionary-proxy exit rules helps out of sample. Zero rule x group cells pass the pre-registered test (positive in both v3b and v4, and BH q < 0.05). The best results are small: on core 30m, CUT05 (hard stop at -0.5R) +0.043R, NP4 (exit if no +0.3R within 4 bars) +0.032R and NP8 +0.021R. All three are positive in both runs but not significant, against a base of -0.146R.
findings.evidence: lens/ai_upside/out/rules_stats.csv. Built by rules_replay.py and rules_stats.py: every SUBMITTED signal run alone through the repo's PaperEngine on 1m live_bars. The base reproduces replay_signals.csv R exactly (max diff 0.0 on 4,236 traded and 410 open signals). Core 30m CUT05: n=639 (v3b 201 / v4 438), 53 hour-clusters, diff +0.043 (v3b +0.082, v4 +0.025), cluster-bootstrap CI -0.019..+0.101, two-sided sign-flip p 0.165, BH q 0.79. NP4: +0.032 (+0.053 / +0.022), p 0.22. 1h CUT05: +0.034, mixed by run (+0.163 / -0.018). Results are the same with open-at-end trades excluded (30m CUT05 +0.054). Lowest BH q anywhere is 0.029, and it is a HURT cell: DeepSeek 15m OPPH -0.061R.
findings.implication: Exit discretion cannot lift any timeframe's base (-0.08 to -0.15R per signal) to break-even. Do not choose AI traders, or AI timeframes, because of exit headroom. At most, put a 30m/1h loss-cut into code as a shadow rule. That is free and needs no Sonnet calls.

findings.claim: Human-style early profit-taking and breakeven moves cost R at 15m. They save the trades that would have hit SL, but they kill more trades that would later have won.
findings.evidence: rules_stats.csv, pooled v3b+v4. Core 15m (n=1,252): BE05 -0.058, TP1 (+1R take-profit, ladder kept) -0.063, PART1 (half off at +1R) -0.031. DeepSeek 15m (n=1,172, v4 only): BE05 -0.082, TP1 -0.095, PART1 -0.048. By run these are mixed: core BE05 is +0.076 in v3b and -0.120 in v4. rule_tradeoff.csv for BE05 on core 15m: it helped 138 trades by +1.24R each and hurt 245 trades by -0.99R each. Break-even needs 44.6% of the changed trades to be helped; the actual share was 36.0%. For TP1 the break-even share is 74.2%; actual 58.3%. disposition.csv: a trade still open 2 bars in at >= +0.3R did better held than exited, by +0.19R (n=334, CI -0.07..+0.40; v3b +0.18, v4 +0.19).
findings.implication: The AI prompt and code should not let a 15m trader take profit or move to breakeven below the ladder's first rung (about +0.86R at 30x). Allow it only after the AI's calls show more than 45% precision against twin code accounts. 'Trade like a human' (take quick profits, hold losers) is the wrong way round here.

findings.claim: One state-based exit was consistent across runs and kinds: at 30m and 1h, a trade still open after 4 bars at <= -0.5R did worse if held than if closed then, by about 0.2-0.3R. This was found after the fact. At 15m the same state gives the opposite sign.
findings.evidence: disposition.csv (exit-now cost included; cluster bootstrap by run x hour). 30m: n=74, hold minus exit -0.220R, CI -0.320..-0.081, p 0.010 (v3b -0.242 n12, v4 -0.216 n62; core -0.231, DeepSeek -0.209). 1h: n=58, -0.287R, CI -0.376..-0.188, p < 0.001 (v3b -0.351, v4 -0.272). 15m: n=202, +0.122, mixed (v3b -0.154, v4 +0.166). The 30m cell surfaced in a scan of about 100 state cells (exit_now_by_state.csv, BH q 0.32), so it counts as a discovery, not a confirmation.
findings.implication: Shadow-test 'close at market if <= -0.5R after 4 bars' at 30m/1h as a code rule; about 11-12% of trades open at bar 4 hit this state. If it holds up, roughly +0.03R per signal sits in code at zero AI cost. It is not a reason to pay for an AI.

findings.claim: Giveback exists but is mostly a 15m effect, and it happens before the ROE ladder arms. 11-15% of 15m signals reach +0.5R and still stop out at about -1.2R. At 30m+ the ladder catches almost every +1R trade.
findings.evidence: giveback_kind_tf.csv, every-signal replay v3b+v4, share reaching +0.5R then SL: core 15m 10.6%, 30m 4.7%, 1h 1.5%; DeepSeek 15m 14.8%, 30m 5.5%, 1h 1.6%. Reached +1R then SL: 0-1.7%. Real trades, all 3 runs: core 15m 8.3% (n=630), DeepSeek 15m 17.4% (n=259). giveback_first_rung.csv: share that reached +1R but closed on the first 10% ROE lock: v3a core 15m 9.5% (50x tier walk), v3b 6.8%, v4 8.6%, v4 DeepSeek 15m 15.1%; those trades kept +0.60..+0.80R of an MFE of 1.12..1.68R. Hindsight upper bounds per trade (perfect breakeven on losers that saw +0.5R, plus cutting dead losers at -0.5R): core 15m 0.24R, 30m 0.15, 1h 0.12; DeepSeek 15m 0.31, 30m 0.19, 1h 0.14. Exiting exactly at MFE: 0.56-0.90R.
findings.implication: The theoretical room for AI exits is largest at 15m (about 0.24-0.31R per trade at most). AIH-1 and AIH-2 show that simple capture of it fails there, so any 15m exit edge would have to come from information beyond the price path. At 30m+ the code ladder already does most of what a human trailing stop would do.

findings.claim: Most losers are dead from the start, and most stop-outs peak in the first 2 bars. Even so, cutting at -0.5R only breaks even at 15m, because it also kills trades that recover.
findings.evidence: time_to_mfe_stop.csv, every-signal base. Losers whose MFE never passed +0.2R: core 45% (15m), 45% (30m), 51% (1h); DeepSeek 48%, 55%, 63%. SL trades whose best price came within 2 bars: 62% / 63% / 77% (core). Median bars to SL: 5.9 (15m), 5.9 (30m), 5.0 (1h); dead SL trades 3.7 / 4.1 / 3.7 bars. Median bars to +0.3R about 1.3-1.5; to +0.5R about 2.6-3.3; reach +1R: 23% (core 15m), 8% (core 30m). Median MAE before +0.5R: -0.26R. rule_tradeoff.csv CUT05 on core 15m: helped 550 trades (+0.49R each), hurt 197 (-1.43R each); break-even precision 74.6%, actual 73.6%. On 30m: 69.1% needed, 74.6% actual.
findings.implication: A 15m AI sees only 3-4 bar closes before a dead trade stops out, and price state alone does not separate dead trades from recovering ones there. At 30m the cut works slightly, because hurt trades lose less (-1.08R vs -1.43R at 15m).

findings.claim: AI exit headroom is a property of the timeframe and of how bad the entries were in that run. It is not a stable property of a strategy. A per-strategy headroom ranking does not replicate.
findings.evidence: headroom_stability.csv, core cells with >= 10 signals in both runs. Spearman of hindsight headroom, v3b vs v4: 15m -0.07 (13 cells), 30m +0.24 (9). v3a trades vs v4 signals: -0.31 (17), -0.52 (9). Per-cell base mean R, v3b vs v4: -0.10 (15m), +0.07 (30m). CUT05 cell gains, v3b vs v4: -0.39 / -0.28. Across cells (headroom_rank.csv), the rule gain is strongly negatively correlated with the cell's base R: CUT05 -0.82 (15m), -0.73 (30m), -0.52 (1h); BE05 -0.87 (15m). Headroom vs base R: -0.60 / -0.42 / -0.86. The core cells with base >= 0 in both runs (N10_HA_PSAR@15m, N17_KC_RSI@15m, N20_EMA9_CHOP@30m, N24_DMI@30m) have headroom 0.08-0.27 and no rule gain in both runs.
findings.implication: Rank AI potential by timeframe, not by strategy. Cells graded H1 ('headroom, rule-consistent') are mostly bad entries being trimmed. Choose AI strategies on entry evidence (5-year results, the side-flip test; other lenses), and treat 'more room for AI exits' as a symptom of bad entries.

findings.claim: Switching to a new signal while in position lost money under every pre-declared policy, in both runs. The loss per switch is about the cost of the extra round trip (about $63 at 30x with margin = 30% of equity), so the replacement signal was no better than the remainder of the held trade.
findings.evidence: switch_sim.py, account-level re-simulation of each account's own signal stream. The base reproduces all 366 accounts' trade counts and closed pnl (max diff $1.2e-10). switch_summary.csv, switch-on-every-new-signal policy: core -$54/switch at 15m (590 switches), -$73 at 30m (257), -$102 at 1h (140); v3b -$50, v4 -$71; 49% of accounts worse vs 16% better. DeepSeek -$28 / -$48 / -$67. Switch only when under water: core -$77/switch (674). Reversal on own opposite signal: core -$210 (26), DeepSeek -$98 (58). Switch only stale trades: core -$72 (114; v3b +$69 on 17 switches), DeepSeek +$3 (122). Signal level (skipped_vs_held.csv): switching to the skipped signal changed equity by -2.07% per instance (core n=1,296, CI -2.69..-1.45; v3b -1.31%, v4 -2.31%), -2.68% when the held trade was under water (n=691), DeepSeek -0.67% (n=1,219). v3a nightly skipped shadows: in-position skips averaged ROE -0.079 vs entered trades -0.037 (15m).
findings.implication: Make 'hold' the default and gate any switch in code. A switch must clear an expected gain greater than one round trip, about 0.22R at 15m and 1.26% of equity at 30x. Do not count switching as an AI upside.

findings.claim: Entering a missed signal 1-4 bars late performs about like entering on time, slightly worse at 15m/30m. Recycling missed signals adds trades at the same (negative) base value, each paying full costs.
findings.evidence: late_lev_summary.csv, same signal re-entered k bars of its timeframe later with a fresh 2 ATR stop (paired). Core 15m: 1 bar late -0.026R (v3b +0.047, v4 -0.059; CI -0.106..+0.058), 4 bars -0.115. Core 30m: -0.045 / -0.086 / -0.065. Core 1h: +0.043 / +0.063 / +0.066 (CIs include 0). DeepSeek 15m: 1 bar late -0.082 (CI -0.159..-0.008), 4 bars -0.151.
findings.implication: Design D12's near-signal and missed-signal entries are unlikely to add edge. If allowed, cap them and score them separately, as the design already plans. They should not be counted as AI headroom.

findings.claim: Leverage changes the exits, because the ladder locks a fixed ROE. On the same signals, higher leverage gave lower R. Above 30x most 15m/30m signals cannot be sized at all under the 2 ATR stop and the 15% max-loss cap.
findings.evidence: lev_pairs.csv, paired fixed leverage with margin = leverage%. 30x vs 20x: -0.026R (core 15m, n=1,252), -0.045 (30m), -0.046 (1h). 40x vs 30x: -0.104 (core 15m, n=976), -0.109 (DeepSeek 15m, CI -0.229..-0.005), -0.135 (DeepSeek 30m, CI -0.282..-0.024). 40x rejected 276 of 1,252 core 15m signals that 30x took; 50x was possible for only 179; at 30m/1h, 40x+ is almost never possible. ladder_geometry.csv: the first lock arms at 1.18 / 0.86 / 0.70 / 0.61R at 20 / 30 / 40 / 50x on 15m (median stop 0.63%), and at 0.84 / 0.61 / 0.50 / 0.43R on 30m. Loss at the stop with margin = lev%: 15m 6.9% of equity at 30x, 19.1% at 50x.
findings.implication: '20-50x by AI confidence' is mostly infeasible above 30x on 15m/30m, and where feasible it quietly tightens the exits. Define the code exits in R (price), not ROE, so a leverage choice does not change the exit. Check whether confidence predicts outcomes (twin accounts) before letting it scale exposure, which grows about 6x from 20x to 50x at margin = lev%.

findings.claim: At 15m, the open trade's P&L state carries no stable exit signal. Whether exiting early would have helped is set by the run's market regime, not by a repeatable state rule.
findings.evidence: exit_now_by_state.csv, hold value minus exit-now value at 1, 2 and 4 bars by unrealized-R bin, with cluster bootstrap: no state cell is BH-significant (min q 0.32). Core 15m, all open trades at 2 bars: v3b -0.17R, v4 +0.22R (opposite signs). Per-cell CIs typically span +-0.3R.
findings.implication: An AI watching only the 15m price path is unlikely to beat code exits. Any 15m exit edge must come from other information (news, order flow, higher-tf context), and must be shown with paired twin accounts, not assumed.

findings.claim: Events and big moves: the window held only one scheduled macro event (NFP 10/02 21:30 KST, v3a), and it did no harm. Entries in or just after the biggest-move hours did better, not worse. Holding against a big move looked costly, but the cluster counts are tiny.
findings.evidence: events_macro.csv: data/macro_events.csv has only NFP 2026-10-02 12:30Z inside the runs. v3a trades entered within 2h: -0.091R (n=163, incl. 5m); trades held through the release +0.48R (n=37); other v3a trades -0.45R. events_bighours.csv, top-decile hours of the 6-coin 1h return (v4: 10/07 00:00, 10:00, 11:00 down, 14:00 up). v4 core signals entered in a big-move hour +0.31R (n=253), the hour after +0.19 (n=241), others -0.14 (n=1,226). v3b: -0.23 / -0.41 / -0.33. events_bighour_hold_vs_exit.csv, positions open at a big hour's end: against the move, hold minus exit -0.13 to -0.36R (core 30m/1h, DeepSeek); with the move +0.15 to +0.78R. Only 3-5 hour-clusters.
findings.implication: Do not build 'avoid volatile hours' logic. A 'cut positions against a big move, keep those with it' reaction is plausible; log it as a code shadow and judge it after many more events (CPI 10/14, FOMC 10/28, PCE 10/29).

findings.claim: Skipping signals because other strategies disagree shows no reliable effect once look-ahead is removed. The naive version, which counts signals up to 15 min after entry, exaggerates the effect.
findings.evidence: agreement.csv, AI-visible window (signals in the 15 min before entry). Conflict minus agree: core 15m -0.019R (CI -0.31..+0.24), 30m -0.152 (CI -0.38..+0.07), 1h +0.049; DeepSeek 15m -0.161 (CI -0.52..+0.17). In v3b, conflict was not worse (15m -0.33 vs -0.41 for agree). agreement_leaky.csv (+-15 min window): core 15m conflict -0.217 vs agree -0.090.
findings.implication: No demonstrated skip rule from cross-strategy agreement. Any replay or evaluation of AI decisions must make sure the AI never sees bars after its decision; the leaky version shows how easily a fake skip edge appears.

findings.claim: Exiting on the strategy's own opposite signal, at the same or a higher timeframe, lowered R at 15m in pooled data (driven by v4). Using reversals as exit or switch triggers is not supported.
findings.evidence: rules_stats.csv, all non-coin-flip kinds, 15m, n=2,424: exit on same-tf opposite signal -0.025R (CI -0.045..-0.009, p 0.004); same-or-higher tf -0.041R (CI -0.074..-0.013, p 0.004). v3b about 0 (-0.001 / +0.014), v4 -0.030 / -0.051. DeepSeek 15m same-or-higher tf -0.061R, BH q 0.029 (the only BH-significant cell in the family). The reversal switch policy lost $98-210 per switch (AIH-7).
findings.implication: Tell the AI not to treat the strategy's own opposite signal as a reason to exit or reverse at 15m/30m.

findings.claim: Ranking by AI headroom: 30m is the only timeframe with a consistent, small exit improvement (about +0.03-0.05R per signal). 1h is similar but is planned as a rule account. 15m has the most theoretical room but nothing that captures it, and the worst costs (about 0.22R round trip). 4h has too few signals.
findings.evidence: Per signal: core 30m CUT05 +0.043, NP4 +0.032, deep-loser cut about +0.22R on about 12% of trades. Core 15m: no rule positive in both runs except NP4 (about 0.000). Trades per account-day (trades_per_account_day.csv): about 4-6 at 15m, 2.3-3.8 at 30m, 1.3-2.9 at 1h. So at 30m the plausible exit gain is about +0.1-0.16R per account-day against a base of about -0.37 to -0.55R per day. Grade counts (headroom_rank.csv), with N meaning too few signals: core 15m H1 3 / H2 12 / L 6 / N 11; core 30m H1 1 / H2 1 / L 12 / N 18; DeepSeek 15m H1 10 (v4 only) / H2 15 / L 1 / N 18; DeepSeek 30m H1 2 / H2 7 / L 9 / N 23.
findings.implication: For the AI budget: if AI traders run at 15m/30m, their value must come from entries and skips (not shown here; see other lenses). Exits should stay code (ladder plus possibly a 30m/1h loss-cut). Prefer 30m over 15m for AI traders. Measure the AI's realized contribution against paired twin code accounts, because the headroom figures are hindsight upper bounds, not expected values.

strategy_notes.numbers: Core 4h: 42 replayed signals (5 in v3b), base +0.068R; 27 of 64 submitted signals rejected by sizing. DeepSeek 4h: 67 signals (v4), base -0.111R. Rule diffs (rules_stats.csv): CUT05 +0.060, NP4 +0.039, own-opposite-signal exits (same tf, and same-or-higher tf) +0.042 each, TP1 -0.044, all within noise (9-11 hour-clusters).
strategy_notes.note: Too few signals to grade any 4h cell. Headroom upper bound about 0.02-0.03R per trade (the ladder arms at about 0.27R at 30x). There is nothing for an AI to work with on exits at 4h.

limits: Runs are very short and cover one market. Replays with paths cover only v3b (0.7 days) and v4 (1.5 days), a quiet, down-drifting market. Core-strategy tests have about 53 hour-clusters and DeepSeek about 37; a regime change could flip any sign.
DeepSeek (ds200) exists only in v4, so none of its results has an out-of-sample check. Its 'H1 (v4 only)' grades are in-sample.

v3a has no live_bars. Giveback for v3a uses only the trade-level MFE/MAE in trades_enriched; rules, timing and switching are v3b+v4 only. v3a also ran at mostly 50x (tier walk), where the ladder locks at a smaller R.

All headroom figures (hindsight upper bounds, exit at MFE) assume perfect hindsight. An AI is not guaranteed any of it, and no AI decisions exist yet to measure. The realized simple-rule results are the only non-hindsight numbers.
Rule exits are checked at 1m resolution and filled at the 1m close with paper slippage (2 bp). An AI that decides at 15m/30m bar closes, or real market exits, would be slower or costlier.

The engine counts the full range of the entry bar in MFE (repo convention), even the part before the fill. This slightly inflates early MFE and shortens time-to-MFE; one artefact is a median of 0.03 bars to +1R for DeepSeek 1h.
The deep-loser cut (<= -0.5R after 4 bars at 30m/1h) was found by scanning about 100 state cells. It replicates in both runs and kinds, but it is a hypothesis for a code shadow, not a confirmed rule.

Switching sims assume the new signal enters at the account's current equity and use the engine's own signal ranking. They cannot represent an AI that picks only its best switches; they show the cost a switch must overcome.
Events: only one scheduled macro event (NFP) fell inside the runs, and the big-move hours number 4-7 per run with 2-5 clusters. Event results are anecdotes.
Fixed-leverage comparisons at 40-50x cover only signals tight enough to be sized (a selected subset); 30m/1h comparisons above 30x are mostly impossible.
Open-at-end trades are marked to the last close (exit costs included). Results are essentially the same with them excluded (rules_stats.csv, resolved_only).

The data cannot tell whether an AI using information beyond the price path (news, order flow, higher-tf context) would capture headroom. That can only be measured with paired twin accounts once the AI runs.
'Near-signal' entries (one condition missing) cannot be evaluated: the export has no near-miss records. Only late entries of real signals were tested.
lens:ai_upside.report_section_md:
## Lens: AI headroom — what human-like discretion could add (early exits, skips, switching, events)

### Bottom line
- **Exits: there is headroom on paper, but the simple discretionary rules did not capture it.** None of the 9 pre-declared rules passed the out-of-sample test (positive in both v3b and v4, and BH q < 0.05). The best was core 30m: cut at -0.5R (CUT05) gained +0.043R per signal, and exit-if-no-progress rules NP4 / NP8 gained +0.032 / +0.021R. These were positive in both runs but not significant, against a base of -0.146R. At 15m, every capture rule was negative or mixed.
- **Early profit-taking and breakeven moves, as a human trader would do them, cost R at 15m**: BE05 -0.06 to -0.08R, TP1 -0.06 to -0.10R. A 15m trader would need more than 45% precision on breakeven calls; the rule achieved 36%.
- **Switching cost about one extra round trip each time**, in every policy and both runs: core -$54 to -$102 per switch, DeepSeek -$28 to -$67, against about $63 for a round trip at 30x with margin = 30% of equity.
- **Missed or late entries perform like on-time ones.** They add trades at the same negative base value, each paying full cost.
- **Leverage changes the exits.** The ladder locks a fixed ROE, so higher leverage locks at a smaller price move. On the same signals, 40x vs 30x lost 0.10-0.14R. At 15m/30m, sizes above 30x are mostly rejected (stop too close to liquidation, or loss at stop above the 15% cap).
- **Headroom belongs to the timeframe, not the strategy.** Per-strategy headroom does not replicate across runs (Spearman about 0), and it is largest where entries were worst. Rank AI potential by timeframe, and choose strategies on entry evidence.

### Method (all numbers from code in `lens/ai_upside/`)
- **Every-signal replay.** Each SUBMITTED signal of v3b and v4 (4,748; reel and 5m excluded) runs alone through the repo's `PaperEngine` on 1m live_bars, with the run's own leverage rule, inferred funding and the inferred brackets. The base reproduces `replay_signals.csv` exactly (R difference 0.0 on 4,236 traded and 410 open-at-end signals).
- **Discretionary proxies.** Each rule is an engine subclass; `engine.py` is unchanged. Rules and tests were written in `PREREG.md` before any run. Already seen beforehand: the summary.md d3 variants (disclosed in PREREG.md).
- **Account-level switching.** Each account's own signal stream is re-simulated. The base reproduces all 366 accounts' trade counts and closed pnl (max difference $1.2e-10).
- **Uncertainty.** Clusters are run x bar close floored to max(timeframe, 1h). Tests use a sign-flip with one sign per cluster plus a cluster bootstrap; BH correction across rule x group cells.

### 1. Giveback and dead entries (every signal, base rules, v3b+v4)

"Gave back" = the trade reached +0.5R and still stopped out. "Dead losers" = losers whose MFE never passed +0.2R. The breakeven, dead-cut, total and exit-at-MFE columns are hindsight upper bounds in R per trade: perfect breakeven on losers that saw +0.5R, cutting dead losers at -0.5R, their sum, and exiting exactly at MFE.

| kind | tf | n | mean R | reach +0.5R | gave back +0.5R→SL | dead / losers | breakeven bound | dead-cut bound | total bound | exit-at-MFE bound |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| core | 15m | 1252 | -0.128 | 59.7% | 10.6% | 45.1% | 0.132 | 0.103 | **0.243** | 0.807 |
| core | 30m | 639 | -0.146 | 53.2% | 4.7% | 45.1% | 0.055 | 0.081 | **0.146** | 0.639 |
| core | 1h | 406 | -0.141 | 40.4% | 1.5% | 50.6% | 0.017 | 0.089 | **0.116** | 0.595 |
| core | 4h | 42 | +0.068 | 21.4% | 0% | 65.0% | 0 | 0.024 | 0.024 | 0.479 |
| ds200 | 15m | 1172 | -0.077 | 65.1% | 14.8% | 47.6% | 0.183 | 0.115 | **0.307** | 0.895 |
| ds200 | 30m | 620 | -0.142 | 55.6% | 5.5% | 54.9% | 0.065 | 0.116 | **0.192** | 0.724 |
| ds200 | 1h | 368 | -0.125 | 44.0% | 1.6% | 62.9% | 0.020 | 0.104 | 0.135 | 0.557 |

Source: `giveback_kind_tf.csv`.

- **Real trades, all three runs:** core 15m gave back +0.5R→SL in 8.3% of trades (n=630); DeepSeek 15m 17.4% (n=259).
- **Reached +1R but exited on the first 10% ROE rung:** v3a 15m 9.5% (50x tier walk), v3b 6.8%, v4 8.6%, DeepSeek 15m 15.1%. These trades kept +0.60..+0.80R of an MFE of 1.12..1.68R (`giveback_first_rung.csv`).
- **+1R then SL is almost absent (0-1.7%)** because the ROE ladder arms at about 0.86R (15m), 0.61R (30m) and 0.44R (1h) at 30x (`ladder_geometry.csv`).

### 2. Timing (bars of the signal's timeframe; `time_to_mfe_stop.csv`)

| kind | tf | reach +0.3R / median bars | reach +0.5R / median bars | reach +1R / median bars | median bars to SL | median bars, dead SL | SL trades peaked ≤ 2 bars |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| core | 15m | 73% / 1.3 | 60% / 2.8 | 23% / 5.7 | 5.9 | 3.7 | 62% |
| core | 30m | 71% / 1.4 | 53% / 3.0 | 8% / 2.8 | 5.9 | 4.1 | 63% |
| core | 1h | 70% / 1.5 | 38% / 3.1 | 8% / 3.0 | 5.0 | 3.7 | 77% |
| ds200 | 15m | 72% / 1.5 | 65% / 3.3 | 31% / 5.7 | 6.9 | 3.5 | 58% |
| ds200 | 30m | 68% / 1.4 | 56% / 2.6 | 15% / 3.3 | 5.1 | 3.2 | 70% |

Median MAE before reaching +0.5R is -0.26R. A 15m AI gets about 3-4 bar closes before a dead trade stops out.

### 3. Pre-declared discretionary-proxy rules: paired difference vs base (R per signal; `rules_stats.csv`)

| rule | core 15m (v3b / v4) | core 30m (v3b / v4) | core 1h (v3b / v4) | ds200 15m | ds200 30m | ds200 1h |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BE05 breakeven after +0.5R | -0.058 (+0.076 / -0.120) | +0.012 (+0.015 / +0.010) | +0.005 (+0.011 / +0.002) | -0.082 | -0.020 | +0.012 |
| BE10 breakeven after +1R | -0.012 | 0 | 0 | -0.002 | 0 | 0 |
| NP4 no +0.3R in 4 bars → exit | +0.000 (+0.031 / -0.014) | **+0.032 (+0.053 / +0.022)** | -0.003 | -0.022 | -0.004 | -0.004 |
| NP8 no +0.3R in 8 bars → exit | -0.024 | **+0.021 (+0.031 / +0.016)** | -0.008 | -0.031 | -0.002 | +0.000 |
| TP1 take-profit at +1R (ladder kept) | -0.063 (+0.027 / -0.104) | -0.020 | +0.004 (both +) | -0.095 | -0.045 | +0.010 |
| PART1 half off at +1R | -0.031 | -0.010 | +0.002 | -0.048 | -0.022 | +0.005 |
| CUT05 hard stop at -0.5R | -0.011 (+0.119 / -0.070) | **+0.043 (+0.082 / +0.025)**, CI -0.02..+0.10 | +0.034 (+0.163 / -0.018) | -0.017 | +0.044 | +0.032 |
| OPP exit on own opposite signal | -0.006 | +0.008 (both +), p 0.035 | -0.006 | -0.045 | -0.006 | -0.005 |
| OPPH same, same or higher tf | -0.022 | -0.006 | -0.006 | **-0.061 (q 0.029)** | -0.016 | -0.004 |

- Base mean R for these groups: core 15m -0.128, 30m -0.146, 1h -0.141; DeepSeek 15m -0.077, 30m -0.142, 1h -0.125. DeepSeek columns are v4 only.
- No cell passes the pre-registered test. The only BH-significant cell is a loss: DeepSeek 15m, exit on own opposite signal at the same or a higher tf.
- Pooled 15m across kinds, exit on own opposite signal: same tf -0.025R, same-or-higher tf -0.041R, both p 0.004 (v4-driven).
- Excluding open-at-end trades changes nothing material (core 30m CUT05 becomes +0.054).

**Why the rules fail (`rule_tradeoff.csv`).**
- Core 15m BE05 saved 138 trades (+1.24R each) and killed 245 (-0.99R each). Break-even needs 44.6% of changed trades to be saved; actual 36.0%.
- TP1 at 15m: needs 74.2%, actual 58.3%.
- CUT05 at 15m: needs 74.6%, actual 73.6%. At 30m: needs 69.1%, actual 74.6%, so it helps a little.

### 4. What the AI sees at its decision points: hold minus exit-now (R; `disposition.csv`, `exit_now_by_state.csv`)

| state | bars after entry | tf | n | hold - exit (95% CI) | v3b | v4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| winning ≥ +0.3R | 2 | 15m | 334 | +0.187 (-0.07..+0.40) | +0.183 | +0.187 |
| winning ≥ +0.3R | 2 | 30m | 101 | +0.033 | -0.027 | +0.041 |
| deep loser ≤ -0.5R | 4 | 15m | 202 | +0.122 (-0.09..+0.40) | -0.154 | +0.166 |
| deep loser ≤ -0.5R | 4 | 30m | 74 | **-0.220 (-0.32..-0.08)** | -0.242 | -0.216 |
| deep loser ≤ -0.5R | 4 | 1h | 58 | **-0.287 (-0.38..-0.19)** | -0.351 | -0.272 |

- **Holding winners beats taking early profit at 15m.** That is the opposite of the human disposition habit.
- **At 30m/1h, cutting trades that are deep under water after 4 bars helped in both runs and both kinds.** This was found after the fact, in a scan with BH q 0.32, so it is a candidate for a code shadow, not a confirmed rule.
- **No other state cell is BH-significant**, and the 15m all-state value flips sign between runs (v3b -0.17, v4 +0.22). Whether early exits help is set by the run's regime, not by a repeatable state rule.

### 5. Switching (account-level re-simulation; `switch_summary.csv`, `skipped_vs_held.csv`)

| policy | core 15m $/switch (n) | core 30m | core 1h | core by run (v3b / v4) | ds200 all tf | mean R of the closed-early trades |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| switch on every new signal | -54 (590) | -73 (257) | -102 (140) | -50 / -71 | -38 (940) | -0.21 |
| switch only when under water | -64 (388) | -86 (175) | -119 (105) | -37 / -91 | -40 (644) | -0.33 |
| switch only stale trades (≥ 4 bars, never +0.3R) | -66 (62) | -60 (35) | -96 (15) | +69 (17) / -96 (97) | +3 (122) | -0.46 |
| switch on same-coin reversal | -267 (17) | +238 (6) | -778 (3) | -444 / -85 | -98 (58) | -0.56 |

- **Signal-level check:** switching to the skipped signal changed equity by -2.07% per instance for core (n=1,296, CI -2.69..-1.45); by -2.68% when the held trade was under water (n=691); DeepSeek -0.67% (n=1,219).
- **v3a nightly skipped shadows:** signals skipped while in position averaged ROE -0.079, against -0.037 for entered trades (15m).

### 6. Late entries and leverage (`late_lev_summary.csv`, `lev_pairs.csv`)

- **Missed signal entered 1 bar late:** core 15m -0.026R (v3b +0.047 / v4 -0.059), core 30m -0.045, core 1h +0.043, DeepSeek 15m -0.082 (CI -0.159..-0.008). Four bars late: core 15m -0.115, DeepSeek 15m -0.151.
- **Same signals at fixed leverage (margin = leverage %):**
  - 30x vs 20x: -0.026 (core 15m), -0.045 (30m), -0.046 (1h).
  - 40x vs 30x: -0.104 (core 15m), -0.109 (DeepSeek 15m), -0.135 (DeepSeek 30m).
  - Feasibility: 40x rejected 276 of 1,252 core 15m signals; 50x was possible for only 179; at 30m/1h, 40x+ is almost never possible.
  - Loss at the stop: at 15m it is 6.9% of equity at 30x and 19.1% at 50x.

### 7. Events and big-move hours (`events_*.csv`)

- **Scheduled events:** only one macro event fell inside the runs, NFP 10/02 21:30 KST (v3a).
  - Trades entered within 2h of it: -0.09R (n=163). Trades held through the release: +0.48R (n=37). Other v3a trades: -0.45R.
- **Big-move hours:** the top decile of the 6-coin 1h return. In v4 these were 4 hours on 10/07 (3 down).
  - Entries in a big-move hour: +0.31R (core, n=253). In the hour after: +0.19R. Other hours: -0.14R.
  - v3b: -0.23 / -0.41 / -0.33.
- **Positions open at the end of a big-move hour:**
  - Against the move: holding was worse than exiting by 0.13-0.36R.
  - With the move: holding was better by 0.15-0.78R.
  - Only 3-5 clusters, so this is an anecdote.

### 8. Skip headroom from cross-strategy agreement (`agreement.csv`)

Signals counted only in the 15 min before entry, which the AI can see. Conflict minus agree:
- core 15m -0.02R (CI -0.31..+0.24)
- core 30m -0.15R (CI -0.38..+0.07)
- core 1h +0.05R
- DeepSeek 15m -0.16R (CI -0.52..+0.17)

v3b shows no difference. A version that also counts signals up to 15 min after entry inflates the 15m effect to -0.13R; it leaks the future and shows how easily an AI evaluation can find a false skip edge.

### 9. Ranking

**By timeframe:**
1. **30m:** small but consistent exit improvements, about +0.03-0.05R per signal, or roughly +0.1-0.16R per account-day at 2.3-3.8 trades/day. The base loses about 0.4-0.55R per day.
2. **1h:** similar, through the loss-cut, but it is planned as a rule account.
3. **15m:** the most hindsight room (0.24-0.31R) and nothing that captures it. Costs are 0.22R per round trip; early profit-taking and breakeven moves are harmful.
4. **4h:** too few signals.

**By strategy:** the per-cell grades in strategy_notes are descriptive only.
- Hindsight headroom does not replicate between runs: Spearman -0.07 at 15m and +0.24 at 30m (v3b vs v4); -0.31 and -0.52 (v3a trades vs v4 signals).
- Rule gains correlate with the cell's base R at -0.52 to -0.87.
- The core cells whose base was ≥ 0 in both runs (N10_HA_PSAR@15m, N17_KC_RSI@15m, N20_EMA9_CHOP@30m, N24_DMI@30m) have little exit headroom (0.08-0.27R) and no rule gain in both runs.
- The cells with the most "capturable" headroom (N12_ICHI_AO@15m, N18_VWMA_MACD@30m, F4_PULL, F16_FIB382, F8_VWICK, F11_TSOUP) are the ones whose entries lost.

### 10. Implications for the AI design
1. **Choose AI strategies and timeframes on entry and skip evidence (other lenses), not on exit headroom.** Prefer 30m over 15m for AI traders.
2. **Keep exits in code (the ladder).** Shadow-test two rules as code before any AI is credited with them:
   - 30m/1h: exit if ≤ -0.5R after 4 bars.
   - 30m: CUT05.
3. **Give the AI three explicit restrictions:**
   - At 15m, no early profit-taking or breakeven moves below the ladder's first rung.
   - No switching unless the expected gain exceeds one round trip (about 0.22R at 15m, about 1.3% of equity at 30x).
   - No exits or reversals on the strategy's own opposite signal.
4. **Define the code exits in R, not ROE,** so that 20-50x leverage by confidence does not silently tighten them. Expect 40-50x to be infeasible for most 15m/30m signals under the 2 ATR stop and the 15% cap.
5. **Measure every AI action against paired twin code accounts.** The headroom here is a hindsight ceiling, not an expected value.

findings.claim: No chart context replicates across runs: when contexts are found in one run and tested in another, the result is no better than chance. In the live data the strategies' chart context carries no structure stable enough for an AI filter to learn.
findings.evidence: Omnibus check, same 63 pre-registered bucket contrasts estimated in v3a and in v4 (core 36). Correlation of the effects across contrasts: 15m +0.092 over 58 contrasts (circular-shift null p 0.514, null 5-95% -0.356..0.462); 30m -0.091 over 49 (p 0.683). Sign agreement 0.586 and 0.592, against null means 0.531 and 0.503 (p 0.32, 0.19). Source: out/omnibus_corr.csv (scan.py). Discovery to test, primary 15m+30m, 2h time blocks, t with df = sum(G-1). Direction A (v3a to v3b+v4): 115 testable, 28 raw p<0.05 (about 6 expected by chance), 15 with BH q<0.10. Out of sample: 3 one-sided p<0.05, 0 with BH q<0.05, 0 replicated, same sign 18/28. Direction B (v4 to v3a+v3b): 108 testable, 7 p<0.05 (about 5 expected), 0 with q<0.10, 1 replicated. Source: out/scan_directional.csv. Winsorized R, win rate and gross R give the same picture: correlation of all effects across runs -0.12..+0.14 (out/robust_directional.csv).
findings.implication: The live paper data gives no basis for an AI 'chart judgement' layer to add the edge the strategies lack. AI traders should not be chosen or justified on the premise that context-aware entries rescue a strategy.

findings.claim: Power is the binding constraint. A single pre-registered bucket contrast can only detect about 0.25-0.6 R, while the real context effects (5-year) are 0.01-0.06 R. A shift of +/-0.4 R is invisible in this sample.
findings.evidence: Median MDE80 (two-sided 5%, 2h-block SE). Core 36, all runs pooled (4.57 days): 15m 0.280 R, 30m 0.240 R. v4 alone: 0.627 R and 0.471 R. ds200 v4: 0.483 R and 0.417 R. After correcting for about 60 contrasts: 0.41 R and 0.35 R. Days of all-strategy signals needed for one pre-specified 0.10 R test: about 36 (15m) and 26 (30m). For the 5-year effect size of about 0.04 R: about 224 and 165 days. Source: out/power_by_scope.csv (analysis2.py). Time clustering is severe: v4 15m design effect 7.4 at 1h blocks, 12.6 at 2h, 19.4 at 4h; v3a 15m 3.7 / 5.7 / 9.1 (out/design_effect_by_block.csv). The known-real cost-channel effect (wide minus tight stop, about +0.15 R) came out at only p 0.10 (15m) and 0.068 (30m) live (out/hypotheses.csv H7).
findings.implication: Paper results before 12/31 cannot validate any context filter, AI-learned or rule-based. Filters have to be designed and validated on the 5-year data. Live paper or shadow can only catch gross breakage. Weekly custom-value tuning of entry filters on a week of shadow data will fit noise.

findings.claim: On 5 years of every-signal data (1.65M signals) the live candidate contexts are real but tiny: a few hundredths of R. The exception is the cost channel (stop width).
findings.evidence: fiveyear_tests2.py, strata strategy x year x side, KST-day clusters. Values are 15m / 30m in R. Europe session -0.039 / -0.021 (z -11.0 / -5.2). ADX>=30 +0.028 / +0.021. Middle of the HTF box -0.030 / -0.013. EMA 'with' +0.024 / +0.008. DI with +0.048 / +0.051. Box far edge +0.057 / +0.044. Range far edge +0.041 / +0.035. Consensus>=4 +0.006 / +0.014. Wide stop +0.163 / +0.102 (z 35 / 18). Signs hold in 4-6 of 6 years (out5y/fiveyear_contrasts.csv). Family hypotheses: trend family in high vs low ER +0.044 / +0.024. Trend family DI with +0.055 / +0.056 (6/6 years). Revert family in low ER -0.005 / -0.003, so no effect. Revert at the 'cheap edge' comes out -0.244 at 15m, the opposite of the prediction (out5y/fiveyear_hypotheses.csv). Live point estimates of the same contrasts were roughly 10x larger: europe 15m -0.415, ADX 15m +0.234 (out/scan_full.csv scope all).
findings.implication: An AI that perfectly learned these contexts would gain about 0.03-0.06 R per kept trade, well below the 0.16-0.22 R median round trip at 15m/30m. Context is a tie-breaker at best, never an edge source.

findings.claim: A learned context filter does not make any strategy break even. Trained on 5-year 2021-08..2024-06 and tested on 2024-07..2026-09, the top third by predicted R improves by only +0.05 R (15m) and +0.03 R (30m) and stays clearly negative. Every one of the 64 core strategy x tf cells keeps a negative filtered mean.
findings.evidence: Ridge on 11 bar-computable context features (out5y/fiveyear_filters.csv, fiveyear_tests.py C11). CF uplift 15m +0.051 R (day-cluster CI 0.039..0.064): kept mean -0.122 vs all -0.173. 30m +0.032 (0.019..0.046): kept -0.087 vs -0.119. The live-trained filter applied to 5 years gives +0.029..+0.059 R per year at 15m (2022-2026) and +0.014..+0.043 at 30m, with kept means -0.08..-0.17 (C10). Per strategy (out5y/fiveyear_filter_by_strategy.csv): best filtered cells are 30m N07_ICHI_CMO -0.032 +/- 0.027, 30m S5_DONCHIAN_MFI -0.041 +/- 0.051, 15m N19_FIB_CHOP -0.083 +/- 0.026. All 64 are below 0. The 15m IS model is dominated by stop width (coefficients: tight -0.17, wide +0.14) (out5y/fiveyear_IS_coefs_15m.csv).
findings.implication: Choose AI-trader strategies on their own direction or exit edge, not on filterability. With these features no 15m/30m core strategy becomes a 'not losing' candidate through context selection.

findings.claim: The largest live 'context' effect is market direction, and it flips between runs. A filter that learns it (with side, coin or session as inputs) loses money out of sample.
findings.evidence: Long minus short at 15m (out/scan_full.csv): v3a +0.694 R (p<0.001); v3b -0.587; v4 core -0.902; v4 ds200 -0.984. At 30m: +0.661, -0.666, -0.599, -0.693. Ridge on all features trained on v3a: in-sample top-third uplift +0.42 R. Out of sample on v3b+v4 core -0.371 R (CI -0.611..-0.144), on v4 ds200 -0.480 (CI -0.749..-0.199) (out/learned_filter.csv). At 15m the 'momentum alignment' contexts are mostly direction in disguise. After stratifying by side: DI-with falls from +0.273 to +0.032, box far edge from +0.325 to +0.028, range far edge from +0.244 to +0.026, EMA-with from +0.305 to +0.166 (out/side_stratified.csv).
findings.implication: A human-like AI that adapts to the last days' winners (longs good, shorts good) will chase the direction of the week. The prompt and memory design should stop the AI from carrying recent-direction lessons into entry filtering and leverage.

findings.claim: A chart-only learned filter (no side, coin or session) transferred weakly across runs: about +0.11..+0.18 R. The bootstrap CIs include 0, and the transfer comes entirely from momentum-alignment features worth only about +0.04 R over 5 years.
findings.evidence: out/learned_filter.csv and out/learned_filter_variants.csv (learned_filter.py, learned_filter2.py). Top third, v3a to v3b+v4: +0.166 R (CI -0.142..0.476; circular-shift null p 0.005; kept mean +0.028 vs -0.138). v3a to v4 ds200: +0.179 (CI -0.254..0.612; p 0.015; kept +0.091 vs -0.088). v4 to v3a+v3b: +0.113 (CI -0.017..0.234; p 0.045; kept -0.194 vs -0.307). Without the 6 momentum features: +0.061, +0.086, +0.002 (null p 0.27, 0.15, 0.37). Stop width alone: +0.009, -0.062, -0.060.
findings.implication: Some transferable structure exists (trade with the short-term move, avoid chasing extended moves), but its true size is about 0.04 R. A 'go with the move' bias is a reasonable soft preference for an AI. It cannot carry a strategy.

findings.claim: Only one contrast passed the strict live out-of-sample test: Europe-session signals (16-21 KST) at 15m. It rests on 5 evenings, and over 5 years it is real but about 10x smaller (-0.04 R).
findings.evidence: Direction B: v4 -0.621 R (n 121), then v3a+v3b -0.322 (n 466), one-sided p 0.002, 4h-block p 0.006, BH q 0.011 (out/scan_directional.csv). The pooled per-run 15m values -0.298 / -0.417 / -0.621 / ds200 -0.405 are all negative. 30m: -0.243 / -0.116 / -0.181 / -0.183 (out/scan_full.csv). Per-evening core 15m differences: 10-02 +0.355 (n 40), 10-03 -0.403, 10-04 -0.229, 10-05 -0.371, 10-06 -0.355 (out/session_episodes.csv). Over 5 years: -0.039 R at 15m and -0.021 at 30m, 6/6 and 5/6 years negative. In ROE only -0.003 (out5y/fiveyear_within_strategy.csv).
findings.implication: Use it at most as a mild tie-breaker (deprioritize 15m entries 16-21 KST), never as a hard rule or a reason to pick strategies. It also shows that live effect sizes are inflated about 10x even when the sign is right.

findings.claim: The owners' entry-quality tier, which already drives 50x 'best' leverage, shows no outcome difference live, in line with the 5-year Study B (0 of 410).
findings.evidence: Quality 'best' minus rest, core 36 all runs: 15m +0.008 R (n 532, p 0.92), 30m +0.070 (n 221, p 0.33). Per run at 15m: -0.018, -0.015, +0.064. 'base' minus rest: 15m -0.069 (p 0.48), 30m -0.112 (p 0.15) (out/scan_full.csv). Within side, 15m best -0.017 (out/side_stratified.csv). Prior: research/entry_study/RESULTS_ENTRY.md, B: 0 of 410 strength tests passed.
findings.implication: Leverage scaled by 'confidence' or quality (20-50x) has no evidential basis from entry features. Leverage tiers should not follow AI or quality confidence, because higher leverage on non-better signals only adds variance and liquidation risk.

findings.claim: Regime-conditional rules ('trend strategies in trend regimes, mean reversion in boxes') cannot even be tested live: trend regimes were nearly absent. Where testable, live and 5-year results do not support them beyond about 0.04 R.
findings.evidence: Regime counts (peek_dist.py): v4 HTF regime at 15m: chop 1,324, box 609, unknown 117, trend 0. Own-tf 15m: trend_down 151, trend_up 0. v3a 15m: 49 trend signals. Live hypotheses H1-H6 (out/hypotheses.csv): smallest BH q 0.29. H6 (revert better in box than chop) went the wrong way: -0.454 R at 15m core (n_box 48). ER contrasts are null live: 15m high +0.012 (p 0.90), low -0.015. DiD 'trend family more ER-sensitive than revert': 15m -0.25 (SE 0.24), 30m +0.31 (SE 0.24) (out/did_er_family.csv). 5-year: H1 +0.044 / +0.024 R, H2 about 0 (out5y/fiveyear_hypotheses.csv). Repo prior docs/regime5y.md: regime switch 0 of 92 cells BH; mean ROE by regime -3.4% to -3.9%.
findings.implication: Do not give AI traders a 'regime gate' as their edge. The current quiet chop market would leave trend strategies idle and not profitable.

findings.claim: The robust 'context' is mechanical cost: signals whose 2 ATR stop is wide relative to the round trip do better in R. In money (ROE) the gain is small.
findings.evidence: 5-year within strategy, wide minus rest: 15m +0.163 R (z 35), 30m +0.102 R (6/6 years). In ROE only +0.003 / +0.006 (out5y/fiveyear_within_strategy.csv). 5-year H7, wide minus tight: +0.264 / +0.144 R (out5y/fiveyear_hypotheses.csv). Live: 15m +0.180 (p1s 0.10), 30m +0.138 (p1s 0.068), v4 15m alone -0.237 (out/hypotheses.csv). Live 15m median 2 ATR stop is 0.59% of price (peek_dist.py). The established median round trip is 0.22 R at 15m vs 0.16 R at 30m.
findings.implication: The defensible custom value is cost-aware: prefer 30m (and 1h) over 15m, and skip or downsize entries whose stop is under about 0.5% of price. Because ROE gains are tiny at fixed margin and leverage, this reduces drag rather than creating profit.

findings.claim: Per-strategy context tests: 25 were testable, 1 survived BH (N18_VWMA_MACD 15m, low-ER signals much worse, consistent across 3 runs). Over 5 years the same contrast is +0.03 R, about 35x smaller.
findings.evidence: out/per_strategy_live.csv (per_strategy.py): 25 testable (at least 10 per side), 2 raw p<0.05, 1 with BH q<0.05. N18 15m high minus low ER: +1.068 R (q 0.00005). Low-ER mean R per run: -1.29 (n 7), -0.39 (14), -0.82 (21); high-ER: -0.28 (88), +0.47 (6), +0.50 (16). Low-ER losers come in bursts (6 BTC/ETH longs within one hour on 10-06). Over 5 years N18 15m: +0.029 R (z 2.0), 30m -0.010 (out5y/fiveyear_hypotheses.csv). The 5-year trend family as a whole: +0.044 R at 15m.
findings.implication: Strategy-specific 'custom' context rules found on days of live data are almost always noise or hugely inflated. A rule like 'skip low-ER signals' for trend strategies has to be sized from 5-year data (about 0.03-0.05 R), not from live data.

findings.claim: No context changes the strategies' direction skill. The side-flip decomposition finds nothing after BH; where a context matters, it matters for both directions (timing or volatility).
findings.evidence: out/sideflip_by_context.csv (analysis2.py, v3b+v4 replay, 216 testable bucket contrasts): R, any-direction mean (R+flip)/2 and direction skill (R-flip)/2 each have 0 with BH q<0.10. Raw p<0.05 counts are 16, 19 and 21 against about 11 expected. Example, middle of the HTF box at 15m core: d_R -0.230, any-direction -0.242 (p 0.002), direction skill +0.012 (p 0.96).
findings.implication: An AI cannot plausibly know in which contexts the strategy's direction call is right. Any contextual benefit is about when to trade at all, which is mostly the cost and volatility channel.

findings.claim: The support/resistance context is nearly constant, so it cannot filter. Consensus or conflict among strategies is noise.
findings.evidence: Share with level_before_lock=1: 85-97%. Share with support_before_stop=1: 96-100%. Median room to the next level 0.22-0.39 ATR (out/signals_bucketed.csv, per run and tf). Repo prior: research/entry_study/RESULTS_ENTRY.md, A: 2 of 290 S/R candidates, both market-wide. Consensus >=4 at 30m: live +0.438 R within side (z 2.4, out/side_stratified.csv) vs 5-year +0.014 (out5y/fiveyear_within_strategy.csv). At 15m: +0.173 live vs +0.006 over 5 years.
findings.implication: Give the AI no weight for 'resistance just ahead' or 'several strategies agree'. Neither is evidence for an entry, and these are exactly the stories a human-like LLM finds persuasive.

findings.claim: Discovery-then-test is not much helped by switching the strategy set either. Contexts found on core 36 (v3a) replicated on DeepSeek (v4) for 1 of 26 contrasts, and that one fails on core 36 in v3b+v4.
findings.evidence: out/scan_directional.csv, direction T: 115 discovery tests, 28 carried, 26 testable, 2 one-sided p<0.05, 1 replicated: 15m middle of the HTF box, v3a -0.335 then ds200 v4 -0.575 (q 0.016, 4h p 0.005). The same contrast on core 36 in v3b+v4: -0.252 (p1s 0.144), and in v3b alone +0.516 (out/scan_full.csv). Over 5 years: -0.030 R (15m) and -0.013 (30m) within strategy.
findings.implication: DeepSeek accounts cannot be graded on context either: 1.5 days, no cross-run replication, no 5-year context data. Treat them as untested.
